Fact.Name: Income source options
Fact.Description: Options describing the source of a member's income.

Fact.Name: Income frequency options
Fact.Description: Options describing how often an income amount is received or anticipated for monthly income conversion (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.402).

Fact.Name: Expense frequency options
Fact.Description: Options describing how often a household expense is billed or incurred when the household elects to average the expense over the period the expense is intended to cover (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407, B).

Fact.Name: Expense type options
Fact.Description: Options describing the type of household expense. Legally obligated child support is captured separately because it is considered an income exclusion (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405, D). Dependent care expense options include care by an individual provider or care facility, transportation to and from the care facility, and activity or other fees associated with necessary dependent care. Shelter expense options are broken out by the allowable shelter-cost categories in 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3, E, including cooling costs for air conditioning systems, room air conditioners, swamp coolers, or evaporative coolers; fans are not allowable cooling costs. Medical expense options include allowable and non-allowable medical cost categories listed for the excess medical deduction in 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.6.

Fact.Name: Resource item type options
Fact.Description: Options describing household resource items, including liquid resources such as cash on hand, money in checking or savings accounts, saving certificates, stocks or bonds, and exempt resources identified in 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.410.

Fact.Name: Pre-purchased funeral agreement exclusion limit
Fact.Description: The maximum equity value excluded for one bona fide pre-purchased funeral agreement per household member; only equity value over one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) is counted as a resource (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.410, D, 4).

Fact.Name: Mileage rate
Fact.Description: The per-mile rate used to calculate dependent care transportation expenses to and from the care facility and reasonable transportation expenses to obtain medical treatment or services, based on the prevailing IRS mileage rate. Effective rate modeled here is seventy cents ($0.70) per mile (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.4; 4.407.6).

Fact.Name: Other excluded income options
Fact.Description: Options for income excluded by other federal statutes under 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405.2. Some options include the qualifying condition in the option name because the exclusion depends on additional facts, such as age, program participation, disaster status, quarterly charitable-donation limits, military deployment status, or statutory tribal/payment limits.

Fact.Name: Other excluded resource options
Fact.Description: Options for government payments received for a specific purpose or services that are excluded as resources for SNAP eligibility under 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.410, J.

Fact.Name: Need-based nonprofit cash donation quarterly exclusion limit
Fact.Description: Maximum aggregate amount of need-based cash donations from private nonprofit charitable organizations excluded per fiscal quarter under 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405.2, A, 10.

Fact.Name: Federal Indian payment exclusion limit
Fact.Description: Dollar limit used by specified federal Indian payment exclusions that exclude only the first two thousand dollars ($2,000) or payments of two thousand dollars ($2,000) or less under 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405.2, B.

Fact.Name: WIOA on-the-job training excluded age limit
Fact.Description: Upper age bound for excluding Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) on-the-job training payments: the participating member must be under nineteen (19) years of age and under the parental control of an adult household member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405.2, A, 6).

Fact.Name: WIOA on-the-job training adult caregiver age minimum
Fact.Description: Minimum age for the adult household member whose parental control qualifies a WIOA on-the-job training payment for exclusion; the participating member must be under nineteen (19) and under the parental control of an adult household member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405.2, A, 6).

Fact.Name: Is presidentially declared disaster or emergency
Fact.Description: Whether there is a major disaster or emergency declared by the President. Disaster or emergency assistance is excluded under 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405.2 only when precipitated by an emergency or major disaster as defined in the Disaster Relief Act; FEMA-funded homeless rent, mortgage, food, or utility assistance when there is no major disaster or emergency is not excluded under this provision.

Fact.Name: Household members
Fact.Description: List of household members

Fact.Name: Incomes
Fact.Description: List of incomes received by household members

Fact.Name: Expenses
Fact.Description: List of household expenses that may be averaged when the household elects to average fluctuating monthly expenses or expenses billed less often than monthly (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407, B).

Fact.Name: Resource items
Fact.Description: List of household resource items whose values are determined as liquid or non-liquid resources at application filing (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.408.1).

Fact.Name: Has inadvertent household error claim due to earned income calculation
Fact.Description: Whether an Inadvertent Household Error (IHE) claim is due to earned income being reported in an untimely manner, so the claim is calculated without allowing the twenty percent (20%) earned income deduction (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Member
Fact.Description: The household member who pays or is legally obligated to pay this expense.

Fact.Name: Member
Fact.Description: The household member who owns this resource item.

Fact.Name: Resource type
Fact.Description: The type of household resource item, including liquid resources such as cash on hand, money in checking or savings accounts, saving certificates, stocks or bonds, and exempt resources identified in 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.410.

Fact.Name: Other excluded resource type
Fact.Description: The specific type of other government payment received for a specific purpose or services and excluded as a resource under 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.410, J. Use when /resourceItems/*/type is Other and the resource matches one of the listed statutory exclusions.

Fact.Name: Is other excluded resource
Fact.Description: Whether this resource item is marked as Other and has a selected government payment type received for a specific purpose or services and excluded as a resource under 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.410, J.

Fact.Name: Resource value
Fact.Description: The countable value of this resource item: for liquid resources, the current redemption rate less encumbrances; for non-liquid resources, the fair market value (or real property value) less verified encumbrances (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.408.1).

Fact.Name: Calculated resource amount
Fact.Description: The resource amount counted after applying resource exclusions. Fully exempt resources count as zero dollars ($0), while a bona fide pre-purchased funeral agreement counts only equity value over one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.410).

Fact.Name: Is liquid resource
Fact.Description: Whether this nonexempt resource item is a liquid resource, including cash on hand, money in checking or savings accounts, saving certificates, stocks or bonds.

Fact.Name: Is countable resource
Fact.Description: Whether this resource item is nonexempt and countable toward household resources after applying the exempt resource types in 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.410.

Fact.Name: Is exempt resource
Fact.Description: Whether this resource item is fully excluded from household resources because it is one of the exempt resource types in 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.410, including vehicles; the home and surrounding property; prorated income; household goods, personal effects, burial plots, life insurance cash value, livestock, retirement accounts, and education accounts; income-producing property; inaccessible resources; resources with no significant return; inaccessible resources of residents of shelters for battered women and children; resources used by or for household members, ineligible non-citizens, or disqualified persons; and specified government payments received for a specific purpose or services. Pre-purchased funeral agreements are handled by /resourceItems/*/calculatedAmount because only equity value over the exclusion limit is counted.

Fact.Name: Is non-liquid resource
Fact.Description: Whether this nonexempt resource item is a non-liquid resource, whose value is determined from the best source available or, for real property, from assessor-reported or assessed value less amounts owed (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1; 4.408.1).

Fact.Name: Expense type
Fact.Description: The type of household expense. Select ChildSupport for legally obligated child support, which is considered an income exclusion (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405, D).

Fact.Name: Amount
Fact.Description: The expense amount at its stated frequency or, when the household does not elect averaging, the monthly expense amount.

Fact.Name: Miles driven to dependent care facility
Fact.Description: The miles driven to and from the dependent care facility at this expense's stated frequency. Mileage expenses are calculated at the stated frequency by multiplying these miles by the dependent care mileage rate, then converted to a monthly amount using the expense frequency (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.4).

Fact.Name: Dependent care transportation mileage amount
Fact.Description: The dependent care transportation mileage expense amount at the expense's stated frequency, calculated by multiplying miles driven to and from the care facility by the dependent care mileage rate (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.4).

Fact.Name: Miles driven for medical treatment
Fact.Description: The reasonable miles driven to obtain medical treatment or services at this expense's stated frequency. Mileage expenses are calculated at the stated frequency by multiplying these miles by the medical mileage rate, then converted to a monthly amount using the expense frequency (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.6).

Fact.Name: Medical transportation mileage amount
Fact.Description: The medical transportation expense amount at the expense's stated frequency, calculated by multiplying reasonable miles driven to obtain medical treatment or services by the medical mileage rate (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.6).

Fact.Name: Amount for monthly conversion
Fact.Description: The expense amount at the expense's stated frequency to use for monthly conversion. Dependent care transportation and medical transportation use the mileage amount calculated from miles driven and the applicable mileage rate; other expenses use the entered amount. Reimbursements are subtracted and floored at zero only for allowable medical expenses (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407, B; 4.407.4; 4.407.6).

Fact.Name: Is necessary dependent care for work, training, or education
Fact.Description: Whether this dependent care expense is necessary for a household member to accept or continue employment, seek employment, or attend training or pursue education that is preparatory to employment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.4).

Fact.Name: Is direct monetary payment outside household
Fact.Description: Whether this dependent care expense is a direct monetary payment to an agency or a person outside of the household. Only direct monetary payments to an agency or a person outside the household are allowable for the dependent care deduction, and in-kind benefits paid to an attendant are not considered (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.4).

Fact.Name: Reimbursement amount
Fact.Description: The amount of this expense reimbursed or expected to be reimbursed from another source at the expense's stated frequency. Allowable medical costs are reduced by reimbursements from another source (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.6).

Fact.Name: Is for claimable shelter residence
Fact.Description: Whether this expense is for a residence whose shelter costs may be claimed by the household: either the household's actual residence, or a home not occupied by the household because of employment or training away from home, illness, natural disaster, or casualty loss where the household intends to return, current occupants are not claiming the shelter costs for SNAP, and the home is not leased or rented during the household's absence (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3, D).

Fact.Name: Is non-utility shelter expense
Fact.Description: Whether this expense is a claimable non-utility shelter expense: it must be for the household's actual residence or a qualifying unoccupied home, and it must be rent, mortgage, condo or association fees, another continuing ownership charge such as qualifying mobile-home purchase loan, reverse mortgage repayment, second mortgage or home-equity loan payment, property taxes, state or local assessments, structure insurance, or qualifying natural-disaster repair or rebuild costs (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3, D-E).

Fact.Name: Is heating or cooling expense
Fact.Description: Whether this expense is for heating fuel or allowable cooling costs for the household's actual residence or another claimable shelter residence. Cooling costs are utility costs relating to the operation of air conditioning systems, room air conditioners, swamp coolers, or evaporative coolers; fans are not an allowable cooling cost (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Incurs or anticipates separate heating/cooling costs
Fact.Description: Whether this heating or cooling expense is incurred or anticipated separate and apart from the household's rent or mortgage (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Private rental billed for heating/cooling
Fact.Description: Whether this heating or cooling expense is for private rental housing and is billed by the landlord on the basis of individual usage, or is charged as a flat rate separately from rent (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Shared residence pays heating/cooling portion
Fact.Description: Whether this heating or cooling expense is for a shared residence where the household incurs at least a portion of the heating or cooling cost, entitling each household to the full Heating and Cooling Utility Allowance (HCUA) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Public housing responsible for excess heating/cooling costs
Fact.Description: Whether this heating or cooling expense is for public housing where the household is responsible for excess heating or cooling costs (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Qualifies for Heating/Cooling Utility Allowance
Fact.Description: Whether this is a heating or allowable cooling expense paid by or billed to a person in the SNAP household and satisfies at least one expense-specific HCUA qualifying condition: separate heating or cooling costs, private rental billing, shared-residence cost sharing, or public-housing excess heating or cooling costs (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Is excluded shelter expense
Fact.Description: Whether this expense is explicitly excluded from allowable shelter costs: separate pet expenses billed apart from rent; unsecured or personal loan payments; insurance for furniture or personal belongings; pay phones; phone cards not associated with a specific device; one-time deposits; internet connectivity fees; or monthly cable/internet fees, including charges bundled with VOIP other than the cost of VOIP itself (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3, E).

Fact.Name: Is dependent care expense
Fact.Description: Whether this expense is an allowable dependent care expense: it must be one of the dependent care expense types (care by an individual provider or care facility, transportation to and from the care facility, or activity or other fees associated with the care provided to the dependent), must be necessary for employment, job search, training, or education preparatory to employment, and must be a direct monetary payment to an agency or person outside the household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.4).

Fact.Name: Is allowable medical expense
Fact.Description: Whether this expense is an allowable medical cost category for the excess medical deduction: the cost must be incurred by a household member who is eligible for the excess medical deduction and must be one of the allowed medical cost categories, including medical or dental care, psychotherapy or rehabilitation services, hospital or outpatient treatment, nursing or nursing-home care, prescription drugs, practitioner-approved over-the-counter medication, medical supplies or equipment, health or Medicare premiums and cost sharing, dentures, hearing aids, prosthetics, eyeglasses, service animal costs, reasonable transportation or lodging for medical treatment, or necessary attendant, homemaker, home health aide, child-care, housekeeper, or attendant-meal costs. Reimbursements are subtracted through the expense amount used for monthly conversion (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.6).

Fact.Name: Expense frequency
Fact.Description: How often this expense is billed or incurred. Weekly, bi-weekly, and semi-monthly expenses are converted to monthly amounts; other non-monthly frequencies are averaged only when the household elects to average the expense over the period it is intended to cover (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407, B).

Fact.Name: Should average expense
Fact.Description: Whether the household elects to average this fluctuating monthly expense or expense billed less often than monthly over the applicable period. This election controls optional averaging frequencies other than weekly, bi-weekly, and semi-monthly, which are converted to monthly amounts regardless of this election (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407, B).

Fact.Name: Months intended to cover
Fact.Description: The number of months this expense amount is intended to cover when the household elects to average an expense over a specific period not represented by another frequency option (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407, B).

Fact.Name: Monthly amount
Fact.Description: The monthly deductible amount of this expense. Dependent care and medical transportation mileage expenses first calculate an intermediate mileage amount at the stated frequency, then use the same monthly conversion rules as other expenses; reimbursements are subtracted only for allowable medical expenses through the amount used for monthly conversion. Otherwise, weekly, bi-weekly, and semi-monthly expenses are converted to monthly amounts. For other non-monthly frequencies, the amount is converted using the selected frequency or divided by the number of intended months only when the household elects averaging; otherwise the stated amount is used without frequency conversion (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407, B; 4.407.4; 4.407.6).

Fact.Name: Legally obligated child support income exclusion
Fact.Description: This member's total monthly legally obligated child support expense, excluded from gross income because legally obligated child support is considered an income exclusion and deducted before applying any ineligible inclusion proration (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405, D; 4.407.3, A).

Fact.Name: Dependent care deduction
Fact.Description: The household's monthly dependent care deduction for allowable dependent care expenses that are necessary for employment, job search, training, or education preparatory to employment and paid directly to an agency or person outside the household. Expenses paid by or billed to a household member are included; expenses paid by or billed to a person disqualified for being an ineligible non-citizen or failing to provide or apply for an SSN are prorated using that person's inclusion ratio; expenses paid by or billed to a person disqualified for IPV/fraud are allowed in full. Reimbursed expenses are not included through /expenses/*/monthlyAmount (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.4).

Fact.Name: Member
Fact.Description: The household member to whom this income belongs

Fact.Name: Income type
Fact.Description: The source/type of this income.

Fact.Name: Other excluded income type
Fact.Description: The specific type of other federally excluded income under 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405.2. Use when /incomes/*/type is Other and the payment matches one of the listed statutory exclusions; several option names include required qualifying facts such as age, program participation, disaster/emergency status, quarterly limits, deployment status, or tribal/statutory payment limits.

Fact.Name: Need-based nonprofit cash donation quarterly exclusion used
Fact.Description: The amount of the three hundred dollar ($300) aggregate fiscal-quarter exclusion for need-based cash donations from private nonprofit charitable organizations that has already been used by other donations in the same fiscal quarter (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405.2, A, 10).

Fact.Name: Indian trust or restricted land interest annual exclusion used
Fact.Description: The amount of the two thousand dollar ($2,000) calendar-year exclusion for income derived from an individual Indian's interest in trust or restricted lands that has already been used by other such income in the same calendar year (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405.2, B, 2).

Fact.Name: Received before SNAP participation
Fact.Description: Whether this income source was received before SNAP participation for exclusions that depend on the income's timing relative to SNAP participation. VISTA payments and earned income tax credits count as income when this is true, and are excluded only when this is false (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405.2, A, 3 and A, 20).

Fact.Name: Is work supplementation or work support public assistance portion
Fact.Description: Whether this income is the portion earned under a work supplementation or work support program that is attributable to a federal, state, or local public assistance program, so it is not eligible for the earned income deduction (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.2, B).

Fact.Name: Is earned income
Fact.Description: Whether this income source is a type treated as earned income: wages and salaries; government payments from Agricultural Stabilization and Conservation Service; VISTA wages; sick leave, vacation pay, and bonus pay while still employed; covered vocational or rehabilitation training allowances; WIOA on-the-job-training earnings; Title I VISTA-University Year of Action payments; self-employment income; LLC or S-Corporation owner income; or boarder income (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.403).

Fact.Name: Is exempt income
Fact.Description: Whether this income is exempt from consideration for SNAP eligibility because it is one of the excluded income sources in 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405, including education assistance received specifically for educational expenses under 4.405.1, or because VISTA payments are excluded when the client was receiving SNAP benefits when they joined VISTA under 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.403.

Fact.Name: Is child student earnings excluded
Fact.Description: Whether this income is earned income of a child under eighteen (18) who lives with a natural, adoptive, or stepparent, or is under the parental control of another household member, and is a student at least half-time in elementary school, high school, or GED classes. This uses the member's K-12 attendance flag to represent elementary/high-school or GED attendance for the child-earnings exclusion (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405, C).

Fact.Name: Is WIOA on-the-job training excluded
Fact.Description: Whether this WIOA on-the-job training payment is excluded because the participating member is under nineteen (19) years of age and under the parental control of an adult household member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405.2, A, 6).

Fact.Name: Is other excluded income
Fact.Description: Whether this income is excluded by another federal statute under 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405.2, either because it is marked as Other with a selected other excluded income type or because it is a WIOA on-the-job training payment excluded for a participating member under nineteen (19) years of age and under the parental control of an adult household member.

Fact.Name: Exempt amount
Fact.Description: The amount of this income that is exempt from consideration for SNAP. Most exempt income is fully exempt; need-based nonprofit cash donations are capped at three hundred dollars ($300) in the aggregate per fiscal quarter, specified federal Indian per-capita payments exclude only the first two thousand dollars ($2,000) or payments of two thousand dollars ($2,000) or less, and income derived from an individual Indian's interest in trust or restricted lands is capped at two thousand dollars ($2,000) per calendar year (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405 and 4.405.2).

Fact.Name: Amount after exemption
Fact.Description: The income amount remaining after subtracting the exempt amount, floored at zero, before monthly conversion.

Fact.Name: Is unearned income
Fact.Description: Whether this income source is a type treated as countable unearned income: assistance payments including SSI, TANF/Colorado Works, and other needs-based assistance; annuities, pensions, retirement, veterans or disability benefits, workers' or unemployment compensation, old age, survivors, or Social Security benefits, and strike benefits; support and alimony; rental income when the household member is not actively managing the property at least twenty (20) hours per week; income of non-citizen sponsors; installment vacation, sick, or bonus pay received after employment terminates; anticipated gifts; other nonexempt income including dividends, interest, royalties, trust withdrawals, and other direct money payments that are a gain or benefit; and substantial lottery or gambling winnings (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.404).

Fact.Name: Amount
Fact.Description: The average income amount for this income at its stated frequency.

Fact.Name: Target pay date
Fact.Description: The date this income was received or is expected to be received, used to test whether terminated-source income was received prior to the date of application and whether new-source income will be received within the applicable tenth-day destitute-income deadline (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.406, A, 1-3).

Fact.Name: Is from terminated source for destitute income
Fact.Description: Whether this income source meets the terminated-source definition for destitute-of-income rules: income normally received monthly or more often that is not expected again from the same source during the remainder of the application month or the following month, or income normally received less often than monthly that is not anticipated in the month it would normally be received (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.406, A, 1).

Fact.Name: Is terminated source for destitute income
Fact.Description: Whether this income was received before the application date and is from a terminated source for the destitute-of-income rules (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.406, A, 1).

Fact.Name: Is from new source for destitute income
Fact.Description: Whether this income source meets the new-source definition for destitute-of-income rules: income normally received monthly or more often but not received from that source within thirty (30) calendar days before the application filing date, or income normally received less often than monthly but not received within the last normal interval between payments (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.406, A, 2).

Fact.Name: Is new source not received within destitute income deadline
Fact.Description: Whether this income is from a new source and its target pay date is after the applicable tenth-day destitute-income deadline, meaning it will not be received by the tenth (10th) calendar day after the filing date for initial certification or by the tenth (10th) calendar day after the household's normal issuance cycle for recertification (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.406, A, 2-3).

Fact.Name: Received this month
Fact.Description: Whether this income is received or anticipated to be received in the month of application; the destitute-of-income source criteria evaluate the household's only income for the month of application (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.406, A).

Fact.Name: Is disregarded for destitute income calculation
Fact.Description: Whether this income is disregarded when the household is destitute of income: for the month of application, destitute households count only income received between the first of the month and the date of application, and income of more than twenty-five dollars ($25) from a new source is disregarded when it will not be received within the applicable ten-day deadline (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.406.1).

Fact.Name: Counts toward destitute income requirement
Fact.Description: Whether this income satisfies the destitute-of-income source requirement: it is from a terminated source received before application, or it is more than twenty-five dollars ($25), from a new source, and will not be received within the applicable tenth-day deadline (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.406, A, 1-3). Household membership, exempt-income, and application-month filtering are applied by /destituteIncomeSourceCriteriaMet.

Fact.Name: Is substantial lottery or gambling winnings
Fact.Description: Whether this income is a single-game lottery or gambling cash prize that equals or exceeds the substantial lottery or gambling winnings threshold (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Income frequency
Fact.Description: How often this income amount is received or anticipated, used to convert the amount to a monthly amount (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.402).

Fact.Name: Months intended to cover
Fact.Description: The number of months this income amount is intended to cover when the income is for another specific period of time; that income is divided by this number of months to obtain average monthly income (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.402.2).

Fact.Name: Monthly amount
Fact.Description: The monthly amount of this income after subtracting any exempt amount, computed by converting the remaining income amount using the pay-frequency conversion rules or, for income intended to cover another specific period of time, by dividing by the number of intended months. When the household is destitute of income, disregarded income is zero and counted income is not converted with monthly multipliers (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.402; 4.402.2; 4.406.1).

Fact.Name: Weekly to monthly conversion multiplier
Fact.Description: Multiplier used to convert weekly average income to a monthly amount: weekly average multiplied by 4.3 (10 CCR 2506-1).

Fact.Name: Bi-weekly to monthly conversion multiplier
Fact.Description: Multiplier used to convert bi-weekly (every two weeks) average income to a monthly amount: bi-weekly average multiplied by 2.15 (10 CCR 2506-1).

Fact.Name: Semi-monthly to monthly conversion multiplier
Fact.Description: Multiplier used to convert semi-monthly (twice a month) average income to a monthly amount: semi-monthly average multiplied by 2 (10 CCR 2506-1).

Fact.Name: Every-other-month to monthly conversion multiplier
Fact.Description: Multiplier used to convert every-other-month average income to a monthly amount: average multiplied by 0.5 (10 CCR 2506-1).

Fact.Name: Quarterly to monthly conversion multiplier
Fact.Description: Multiplier used to convert quarterly average income to a monthly amount: average multiplied by 0.333333 (10 CCR 2506-1).

Fact.Name: Twice-a-year to monthly conversion multiplier
Fact.Description: Multiplier used to convert twice-a-year average income to a monthly amount: average multiplied by 0.166666 (10 CCR 2506-1).

Fact.Name: Annual to monthly conversion multiplier
Fact.Description: Multiplier used to convert annual average income to a monthly amount: average multiplied by .083 (10 CCR 2506-1).

Fact.Name: ABAWD work type options
Fact.Description: Options describing whether job hours count as ABAWD work: compensated work, in-kind work, unpaid work verified by the provider of the unpaid work, or other work that does not count toward the ABAWD work requirement (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Jobs
Fact.Description: List of jobs held by household members for SNAP employment and work-requirement determinations.

Fact.Name: Federal minimum wage hourly rate
Fact.Description: The federal minimum wage hourly rate in effect beginning July 24, 2009.

Fact.Name: Member
Fact.Description: The household member who holds this job.

Fact.Name: Hours per week
Fact.Description: The average number of hours per week worked in this job. Employed or self-employed individuals may be exempt from SNAP work requirements when they work at least thirty (30) hours per week (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: ABAWD work type
Fact.Description: The type of work performed in this job for ABAWD work-requirement purposes. Compensated work, in-kind work, and unpaid work verified by the provider of the unpaid work count toward ABAWD work hours (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Is self-employed
Fact.Description: Whether this job is self-employment. The work-requirement employment exemption applies to employed or self-employed individuals who meet the hours or weekly-earnings threshold (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Is at federal minimum wage
Fact.Description: Whether this job is paid at least the federal minimum wage for the hours worked. For self-employment, this means earnings after allowable business expenses are deducted are at least equal to the federal minimum wage for the hours worked. Used to add up hours that count toward the student self-employment wage requirement and the work-requirement employment earnings threshold (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, B; 4.310).

Fact.Name: Is on-the-job training
Fact.Description: Whether this job is on-the-job training (OJT), meaning training provided to an employee after they are hired and designed for individuals who do not have the necessary work experience required for the job (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Employment is suitable
Fact.Description: Whether this offered employment is suitable for the member. Employment is considered suitable unless wages are below the applicable federal or state minimum wage (or eighty percent of the federal minimum wage if neither applies), piece-rate expected hourly yield is below that wage, the job requires joining, resigning from, or refraining from joining a legitimate labor organization, the worksite is subject to a strike or lockout that has not been enjoined, health and safety risk is unreasonable, the member is physically or mentally unfit for the job, the job is outside the member's major field of experience during the first thirty (30) days after registration while opportunities in that field have not been offered, distance is unreasonable considering wage and commute time/cost, daily commuting time exceeds two (2) hours excluding child-care transportation, the distance prohibits walking and no public or private transportation is available, or the working hours or nature of employment interferes with the member's religious observances, convictions, or beliefs (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310.7).

Fact.Name: Offer accepted
Fact.Description: Whether the member accepted this offered job.

Fact.Name: Wages below applicable minimum
Fact.Description: Whether the wages offered for this employment are less than the higher of the applicable federal or state minimum wage, or less than eighty percent (80%) of the federal minimum wage if neither the federal nor state minimum wage is applicable (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310.7).

Fact.Name: Piece-rate yield below applicable wage
Fact.Description: Whether this employment is offered on a piece-rate basis and the average hourly yield the employee can reasonably be expected to earn is less than the applicable hourly wage for suitable employment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310.7).

Fact.Name: Requires labor organization action
Fact.Description: Whether the member is required, as a condition of this employment, to join, resign from, or refrain from joining any legitimate labor organization (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310.7).

Fact.Name: Worksite subject to strike or lockout
Fact.Description: Whether this employment is at a site subject to a strike or lockout at the time of the offer, unless the strike has been enjoined under the Labor Management Relations Act or Railway Labor Act (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310.7).

Fact.Name: Unreasonable health or safety risk
Fact.Description: Whether the member can demonstrate, or the local office becomes aware, that this employment presents an unreasonable degree of risk to health and safety (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310.7).

Fact.Name: Member physically or mentally unfit
Fact.Description: Whether the member is physically or mentally unfit to perform this employment, as established by documentary medical evidence or reliable information obtained from other sources (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310.7).

Fact.Name: Outside major field during initial thirty days
Fact.Description: Whether this employment is not in the member's major field of experience and job opportunities in that major field have not failed to be offered after thirty (30) calendar days from registration (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310.7).

Fact.Name: Unreasonable distance
Fact.Description: Whether the distance from the member's home to the place of employment is unreasonable considering the expected wage and the time and cost of commuting (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310.7).

Fact.Name: Daily commute exceeds two hours
Fact.Description: Whether the daily commuting time for this employment exceeds two (2) hours per day, not including the time needed to transport a child or children to and from a child care facility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310.7).

Fact.Name: No transportation for non-walking distance
Fact.Description: Whether the distance to the place of employment prohibits walking and neither public nor private transportation is available to transport the member to the job site (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310.7).

Fact.Name: Interferes with religious observance
Fact.Description: Whether the working hours or nature of this employment interferes with the member's religious observances, convictions, or beliefs (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310.7).

Fact.Name: Caregiver relationships
Fact.Description: List of parent-or-caregiver relationships between household members. Each entry links one adult to one child and covers either (a) a natural, adoptive, or stepparent relationship or (b) a non-parent household member who exercises parental control over the child. A single child may appear in multiple entries (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Caregiver
Fact.Description: The household member who is either a natural, adoptive, or stepparent in this relationship, or a non-parent household member exercising parental control over the child. When the relationship is a natural, adoptive, or stepparent relationship to a child aged twenty-one (21) years or younger living in the same home, this member must be included in the SNAP household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Dependent
Fact.Description: The household member who is the child or dependent in this caregiver relationship — either the natural, adoptive, or stepchild of the caregiver, or a child under the parental control of a non-parent household member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is parent relationship
Fact.Description: Whether the caregiver-side member is the child's natural, adoptive, or stepparent, rather than a non-parent household member exercising parental control over the child. A child under eighteen (18) is considered to be under parental control of a household member when financially or otherwise dependent on that member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is non-parent parental-control relationship
Fact.Description: Whether this caregiver relationship is the non-parent parental-control kind: the dependent-side member is a child under the parental control of a caregiver-side member who is not the child's natural, adoptive, or stepparent. A child under eighteen (18) is considered to be under parental control of a household member when financially or otherwise dependent on that member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Caregiver provides more than half of physical care
Fact.Description: Whether the caregiver-side member in this relationship is responsible for more than half of the physical care of the child. Used by the SNAP student-eligibility exemption for a student responsible for the physical care of a dependent household member aged six (6) to under twelve (12) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, E).

Fact.Name: Adequate childcare is unavailable
Fact.Description: Whether the local office has determined that adequate childcare is not available for the dependent-side member in this relationship to enable the caregiver-side member to attend class and satisfy the requirement of item B or item C of 4.306.1 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, E).

Fact.Name: Claimed for work-requirements care exemption
Fact.Description: Whether this caregiver relationship is the one claimed for the SNAP work-requirements exemption for a parent or other household member responsible for the care of this dependent child under six (6) or incapacitated person. This per-relationship flag identifies which caregiver claims the exemption when multiple caregivers are associated with the same dependent (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Age
Fact.Description: Age of this member in years. If their birthday occurs in the middle of a month, use the age they were when the month began (the last day of the previous month).

Fact.Name: Has physical disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member has a physical disability

Fact.Name: Has mental disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member has a mental disability

Fact.Name: Is incapacitated
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an incapacitated person whose care may qualify one parent or other household member for the SNAP work-requirements exemption (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Receives SSI or disability/blindness payments
Fact.Description: Whether this member receives Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits under Title XVI of the Social Security Act, or the Colorado Supplement, or Aid to the Needy and Disabled-Supplemental Security Income-Colorado Supplement (AND-SSI-CS), or Aid to the Blind-Supplemental Security Income-Colorado Supplement (AB-SSI-CS); or Disability or Blindness Payments under Title I, II, X, or IXV of the Social Security Act (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is veteran with service-connected or non-service-connected disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a veteran with a service-connected disability rated or paid as a total disability under Title 38 of the United States Code, or is a veteran receiving a pension for a non-service-connected disability (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is veteran needing aid and attendance or permanently housebound
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a veteran considered by the Veterans Affairs (VA) to be in need of regular aid and attendance or permanently housebound under Title 38 of the United States Code (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is veteran's surviving spouse or child needing aid and attendance
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a surviving spouse of a veteran and considered in need of aid and attendance or permanently housebound, or a surviving child of a veteran and considered by the VA to be permanently incapable of self-support under Title 38 of the United States Code (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is veteran's surviving spouse or child with permanent disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a surviving spouse or child of a veteran considered by the VA to be entitled to compensation for a service-connected death or pension benefits for a non-service-connected death under Title 38 of the United States Code, and has a disability considered permanent under Section 221(i) of the Social Security Act. "Entitled" refers to those veterans' surviving spouses and children who are receiving the compensation or benefits or have been approved for such benefits but are not yet receiving them (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Receives public disability retirement pension
Fact.Description: Whether this member has a disability considered permanent under Section 221(i) of the Social Security Act and receives a federal, state, or local public disability retirement pension (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Receives railroad retirement disability annuity
Fact.Description: Whether this member receives an annuity for disability from the railroad retirement board and is considered as a person with disabilities by the SSA, or qualifies for Medicare as determined by the railroad retirement board (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Receives interim assistance pending SSI/disability benefits
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a recipient of interim assistance benefits pending the receipt of Supplemental Security Income (SSI), disability-related medical assistance under Title XIX of the Social Security Act, or disability-based state assistance benefits, provided that eligibility for those benefits is based on disability or blindness criteria at least as stringent as those used under Title XVI of the Social Security Act (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is person with disabilities
Fact.Description: Whether this member meets any of the criteria defining a "person with disabilities" under SNAP: receipt of SSI or other disability/blindness payments; veteran status with a service-connected or non-service-connected disability; veteran needing aid and attendance or permanently housebound; surviving spouse or child of a veteran needing aid and attendance or permanently incapable of self-support; surviving spouse or child of a veteran with a permanent disability; permanent disability with a public disability retirement pension; railroad retirement disability annuity; or interim assistance pending SSI or disability-based benefits (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is boarder
Fact.Description: Whether this member resides with others and pays reasonable compensation to others for lodging and meals (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is roomer
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an individual to whom a household furnishes lodging, but not meals, for compensation (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Lives in boarding house
Fact.Description: Whether this member lives in an establishment that is licensed as a commercial enterprise and which offers meals and lodging for compensation, as described in 7 C.F.R 273.1(b)(3)(i) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Lives in an institution
Fact.Description: Whether this member lives in a place which has not been authorized by FNS to accept SNAP benefits, but which provides its residents with more than fifty percent (50%) of their daily meals as part of its normal services. Residents of a halfway house for persons with a disability are residents of an institution if they are provided meals as part of their regular service. Students who purchase meal plans through an institution of higher education are residents of an institution if the meal plan provides them more than fifty percent (50%) of their meals (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.4)

Fact.Name: Lives in federally subsidized housing for persons aged 60 and older
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a resident of federally subsidized housing for persons aged sixty (60) and older under 12 U.S.C. 1701Q or 12 U.S.C. 1715Z-1 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.41)

Fact.Name: Resides at a drug or alcohol treatment and rehabilitation facility
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a narcotic addict or alcoholic, or the child of one, who resides at a facility or treatment center for purposes of regular participation in a drug or alcoholic treatment and rehabilitation program (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.41)

Fact.Name: Resident of a homeless shelter
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a resident of a public or private nonprofit shelter for the homeless (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.41)

Fact.Name: Exempt from boarding house or institution disqualification
Fact.Description: Whether this member, although a resident of a boarding house or institution, qualifies for an exemption under Section 4.304.41 that allows them to participate in SNAP. The exemptions are: (A) resident of federally subsidized housing for persons aged 60 and older under 12 U.S.C. 1701Q or 1715Z-1; (B) narcotic addicts or alcoholics and their children residing at a drug or alcohol treatment and rehabilitation facility; (C) blind or disabled residents of a public or private nonprofit group living arrangement facility; (D) women, or women and their children, temporarily residing in a public or private nonprofit shelter for battered women and children; (E) residents of public or private nonprofit shelters for the homeless (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.41)

Fact.Name: Prepares food with household
Fact.Description: Whether this member customarily purchases and prepares food together with the rest of the household for home consumption (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Lives in group living arrangement
Fact.Description: Whether this member lives in a public or private non-profit facility certified under Section 1616(e) of the Social Security Act which serves no more than sixteen (16) people (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is live-in attendant
Fact.Description: Whether this member resides with the household to provide child-care or other personal services (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is separate and apart
Fact.Description: Whether this member, who would otherwise be a mandatory household member, has established a residence separate and apart from the other mandatory household members. A residence is only considered established as separate and apart when the individual pays shelter expenses, supports the maintenance of the other residence (e.g., paying rent/mortgage, utilities, insurance, or other charges necessary to maintain the residence), or has provided that separate address to other governmental organizations or an employer as their primary residence. When true, the member is not required to be considered part of the SNAP household, and any monies that person provides to the SNAP household should be considered unearned income (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory household member
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a mandatory household member who must be considered in the same household as the other mandatory individuals they live with, even if they declare they do not customarily purchase and prepare their food together for home consumption. Mandatory members include the designated head of household, anyone in a spouse relationship with another household member, any mandatory child, any parent of a mandatory child living in the same home, and any person aged sixty (60) or older with a disability who is unable to purchase and prepare their own meals and lives with others whose income exceeds 165% of the federal poverty line (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.203, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is optional household member
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an optional household member who resides with the household but shall not be considered a household member in determining the household's eligibility or allotment, unless otherwise stated. True when this member is eligible to be in a separate household as a person aged sixty (60) or older with a disability whose food-preparation-group co-residents' combined income does not exceed 165% of the federal poverty line, when this member is a foster child whom the foster parent may choose to include in or exclude from the SNAP household, or when this member is a boarder whom the household may choose to include as a household member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1, 4.304.3).

Fact.Name: Is boarder
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a boarder of the client's household. Boarders are only considered members of a client's SNAP household if the household requests that they be considered household members (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is non-household member
Fact.Description: Whether this member resides with the household but shall not be considered a household member in determining the household's eligibility or allotment, unless otherwise stated in 4.304.3. True when this member is a roomer or a live-in attendant. Boarders are excluded here because they are essentially optional household members — see /members/*/isOptionalHouseholdMember (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.31).

Fact.Name: Is part of household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is part of the SNAP household — a group of individuals who live together and customarily purchase and prepare food together for home consumption. Mandatory household members are always considered part of the household regardless of food preparation. A member who would otherwise be part of the household but has established a residence separate and apart (/members/*/isSeparateAndApart) is excluded. A person who is a non-household member under /members/*/isNonHouseholdMember, or who is an ineligible student for SNAP purposes, is treated as outside the household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304, 4.304.1, 4.304.31, 4.306).

Fact.Name: Is head of household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is the head of the SNAP household — the person to whom the local office addresses correspondence and notices about the household's case, generally the individual who completes the application process and is responsible for obtaining and using the household's EBT card (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304).

Fact.Name: Spouse
Fact.Description: The household member who is this member's spouse — either a person married to this member under state law, or a person living together with this member who is free to marry and is representing themselves as a spouse to relatives, friends, neighbors, or the larger community (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory spouse
Fact.Description: Whether this member is in a spouse relationship with another member of the household who is themselves part of the SNAP household. True when this member's spouseId references a household member who is part of the household, or when another member who is part of the household identifies this member as their spouse. Spouses must always be considered part of the same SNAP household regardless of whether they purchase and prepare food together (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is emancipated minor
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a minor who has been emancipated as defined by state law. An emancipated minor is not considered to be under another household member's parental control for purposes of the mandatory-child SNAP household rule (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is foster child
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a foster child. Foster children are explicitly excluded from the rule requiring a child under eighteen (18) who lives under the parental control of a non-parent household member to be a mandatory household member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Mandatory child age limit (parent case)
Fact.Description: Upper bound (inclusive) on a child's age for the first mandatory-child SNAP household case: a person aged twenty-one (21) years or younger living with their natural, adoptive, or stepparent (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Mandatory child age limit (parental control case)
Fact.Description: Upper bound (exclusive) on a child's age for the second mandatory-child SNAP household case: a non-foster, non-emancipated child under eighteen (18) years of age living with and under the parental control of a non-parent household member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory child via parent in household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a mandatory household member under the first mandatory-child case: a person aged twenty-one (21) years or younger who has at least one /caregiverRelationships entry whose caregiver-side member is part of the SNAP household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory child via non-parent parental control
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a mandatory household member under the second mandatory-child case: a non-foster, non-emancipated child under eighteen (18) years of age who has at least one /caregiverRelationships entry where the child is under parental control of the caregiver-side member and that caregiver-side member is part of the SNAP household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory child household member
Fact.Description: Whether this member must be included in the SNAP household as the child of, or a child under the parental control of, another household member. True when either /members/*/isMandatoryChildViaParent or /members/*/isMandatoryChildViaParentalControl is true (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory parent via child in household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a mandatory household member under the caregiver-side mirror of the first mandatory-child case: a natural, adoptive, or stepparent (i.e., the linked /caregiverRelationships entry has isParent true) of a household member aged twenty-one (21) years or younger who is themselves part of the SNAP household. Uses dependentId/isPartOfHousehold on the dependent side so the existence-in-household check matches the policy phrasing "living with their natural or adoptive parent(s) or stepparent(s)" (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory parent via non-parent parental control
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a mandatory household member under the caregiver-side mirror of the second mandatory-child case: a non-parent caregiver with parental control over a non-foster, non-emancipated child under eighteen (18) years of age who is themselves part of the SNAP household. Uses dependentId/isPartOfHousehold on the dependent side so the existence-in-household check matches the policy phrasing "living with…a household member" (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is mandatory parent household member
Fact.Description: Whether this member must be included in the SNAP household as the parent of, or a non-parent caregiver exercising parental control over, a child who is themselves part of the SNAP household. True when either /members/*/isMandatoryParentViaChild or /members/*/isMandatoryParentViaParentalControl is true (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Is unable to purchase and prepare own meals due to a disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member is experiencing a disability and, as a result of that disability, is unable to purchase and prepare their own meals. Used together with age sixty (60) or older to determine when the member must be considered part of the same SNAP household as the others they live with (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Others in food-prep group have income exceeding 165% FPL
Fact.Description: Whether the combined income of every other member of this member's food-preparation group exceeds 165% of the federal poverty level for a household size equal to the food-preparation group's size minus this member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1). Placeholder pending the income calculation work.

Fact.Name: Is mandatory elderly member with disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member must be included in the SNAP household under the rule that a person aged sixty (60) or older who is also experiencing a disability, is unable to purchase and prepare their own meals, prepares food with the rest of the household, and is residing with other individuals whose combined income exceeds 165% of the federal poverty line (for the food-preparation group's size excluding this member) must be in the same household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Can be separate elderly-with-disability household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is eligible to be considered a separate SNAP household under the rule that a person aged sixty (60) or older who is also experiencing a disability, is unable to purchase and prepare their own meals, and is residing with other individuals whose combined income does not exceed 165% of the federal poverty line (for the food-preparation group's size excluding this member) can be in a separate household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.1).

Fact.Name: Has ABAWD disability
Fact.Description: Whether this member has a physical or mental disability that disqualifies them from ABAWD status (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: ABAWD minimum age
Fact.Description: Lower bound (inclusive) of the ABAWD age range (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: ABAWD maximum age
Fact.Description: Upper bound (inclusive) of the ABAWD age range (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: ABAWD dependent age limit
Fact.Description: A household member younger than this age disqualifies others from ABAWD status (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Under ABAWD dependent age limit
Fact.Description: Whether this member is younger than the ABAWD dependent age limit

Fact.Name: Has member under ABAWD dependent age limit
Fact.Description: Whether the household contains anyone younger than the ABAWD dependent age limit

Fact.Name: Is ABAWD
Fact.Description: Able-Bodied Adult Without Dependents: aged 18 through 54, without a physical or mental disability, in a household with no one under 18 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Application filing date
Fact.Description: The date an application for public assistance is received by the county office, used as the application date for destitute-of-income timing (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1; 4.406)

Fact.Name: Application for recertification
Fact.Description: Whether this application was submitted prior to the last month of the certification period to determine the household's continued eligibility for the next certification period (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Normal issuance cycle date
Fact.Description: The household's normal issuance cycle date, used for recertification applications when determining whether new-source income will be received by the tenth (10th) calendar day after that normal issuance cycle for destitute-of-income treatment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.406, A, 2-3).

Fact.Name: Application month start date
Fact.Description: The first day of the month of application, used to determine which income is counted for destitute households because eligibility and benefit levels are calculated using only income received between the first of the month and the date of application (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.406.1).

Fact.Name: Allotment
Fact.Description: The total amount of SNAP benefits the household is authorized to receive in a particular month, computed by rounding the unfloored allotment down to the nearest dollar, then raising it up to the federal minimum allotment for one- and two-person households (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Unfloored allotment
Fact.Description: The household's SNAP benefit allotment before rounding down to the nearest dollar or applying the minimum-benefit rule, computed as the maximum allotment for the household size minus thirty percent (30%) of net monthly income (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Expected contribution rate
Fact.Description: The share of net monthly income the household is expected to contribute toward its food costs, used to compute the SNAP benefit allotment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Expected contribution
Fact.Description: The portion of the household's net monthly income that the household is expected to contribute toward its food costs, which is subtracted from the maximum allotment to determine the SNAP benefit (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Household size
Fact.Description: The number of non-disqualified members who are part of the household, used to look up the maximum monthly SNAP allotment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3; 4.304.4).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 1-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 1-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 2-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 2-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 3-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 3-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 4-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 4-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 5-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 5-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 6-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 6-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 7-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for a 7-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment for 8-person household
Fact.Description: Maximum monthly SNAP allotment for an 8-person household, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment per additional person
Fact.Description: The amount added to the 8-person maximum monthly SNAP allotment for each additional household member beyond eight, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3).

Fact.Name: Maximum allotment
Fact.Description: The maximum monthly SNAP allotment for the household, derived from the cost of the thrifty food plan as defined by the FNS. The cost of that diet is the basis for uniform allotments for all households regardless of their actual composition (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Looked up from the household-size schedule effective October 1, 2025, with /maxAllotmentPerAdditionalPerson added for each member beyond eight.

Fact.Name: Days in application month
Fact.Description: The last day of the calendar month in which the household applied for benefits; use /daysInApplicationMonth/day to obtain the exact number of days in that month (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.2).

Fact.Name: Application day of month
Fact.Description: The day of the month on which the household submitted its application for benefits (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.2).

Fact.Name: Is migrant or seasonal farm worker
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a migrant or seasonal farm worker who is in the job stream and whose break in participation does not exceed thirty (30) days (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.2).

Fact.Name: Has migrant or seasonal farm worker
Fact.Description: Whether the household contains any migrant or seasonal farm worker who is in the job stream (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.2).

Fact.Name: Received SNAP in the last 30 days
Fact.Description: Whether the household received SNAP benefits within the thirty (30) days preceding the current application. Used to determine whether a migrant or seasonal farm worker household's break in participation does not exceed thirty (30) days, which exempts the household from initial-month allotment proration (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.2).

Fact.Name: Prorated allotment
Fact.Description: The household's SNAP benefit level for the initial month of application, rounded down to the nearest dollar. If the calculation of benefits for the initial month yields an allotment of less than the federal minimum allotment, no benefits are issued to the household for the initial month (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.3 B).

Fact.Name: Unfloored prorated allotment
Fact.Description: The household's initial-month allotment before rounding down to the nearest dollar or applying the minimum-benefit cutoff, computed using the exact number of days in the calendar month: ((days in month + 1) - date of application) * full month's unfloored allotment / days in the application month. Migrant or seasonal farm worker households in the job stream whose break in participation does not exceed thirty (30) days are exempt from proration and receive the full month unfloored allotment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.207.2).

Fact.Name: Minimum allotment
Fact.Description: The minimum amount of benefits issued to one- and two-person households that are eligible for assistance, but whose issuance calculates to less than the federally prescribed minimum allotment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1). Effective October 1, 2025, the minimum monthly allotment for 1-2 person households is $24.

Fact.Name: Utility allowance category options
Fact.Description: The standard utility allowance categories available for determining a household's excess shelter deduction under 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31, including the telephone allowance for households whose only utility cost is telephone service, plus None when no utility allowance applies.

Fact.Name: Utility allowance category
Fact.Description: The one mandatory standard utility allowance category the household is entitled to use for utility costs; households cannot claim actual utility expenses and are entitled to only one allowance. HCUA applies first; BUA applies to households not entitled to HCUA that incur at least two non-heating or non-cooling utility costs; the telephone allowance applies when telephone service is the household's only utility cost category; and OUA applies to households not entitled to HCUA or BUA that are responsible for only one non-heating or non-cooling utility expense other than telephone (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Basic Utility Allowance
Fact.Description: The fixed Basic Utility Allowance (BUA) standard applied to households that are not entitled to the HCUA and that incur at least two non-heating or non-cooling utility costs, such as electricity, water, sewer, trash, cooking fuel, or telephone. Effective October 1, 2025, the BUA standard is $377 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Heating/Cooling Utility Allowance
Fact.Description: The fixed heating and cooling utility allowance (HCUA) standard applied to households that qualify for the HCUA. Effective October 1, 2025, the HCUA standard is $594 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has Heating/Cooling Utility Allowance
Fact.Description: Whether the household qualifies for the HCUA because it received a LEAP or E-EBT payment within the previous twelve (12) months, or because it has at least one heating or allowable cooling expense paid by or billed to a person in the SNAP household that satisfies an expense-specific HCUA qualifying condition: separate heating or cooling costs, private rental billing, shared-residence cost sharing, or public-housing excess heating or cooling costs (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has BUA electricity expense
Fact.Description: Whether the household has at least one Basic Utility Allowance (BUA)-countable electricity expense for non-heating and non-cooling use (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has BUA water expense
Fact.Description: Whether the household has at least one Basic Utility Allowance (BUA)-countable water expense (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has BUA sewer expense
Fact.Description: Whether the household has at least one Basic Utility Allowance (BUA)-countable sewer expense (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has BUA trash expense
Fact.Description: Whether the household has at least one Basic Utility Allowance (BUA)-countable garbage or trash collection expense (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has BUA cooking fuel expense
Fact.Description: Whether the household has at least one Basic Utility Allowance (BUA)-countable cooking fuel expense (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has BUA telephone expense
Fact.Description: Whether the household has at least one Basic Utility Allowance (BUA)-countable telephone expense. Landline, cellular, disposable cell phone, and VOIP service are grouped as one telephone category (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has BUA supplemental heating expense
Fact.Description: Whether the household has at least one Basic Utility Allowance (BUA)-countable supplemental heating source expense. Space heaters, electric blankets, heat lamps, and cooking stoves used for heat are grouped as one supplemental-heating category and do not qualify the household for HCUA (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has BUA well installation or maintenance expense
Fact.Description: Whether the household has at least one Basic Utility Allowance (BUA)-countable well installation or maintenance expense that is the household's responsibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has BUA septic tank installation or maintenance expense
Fact.Description: Whether the household has at least one Basic Utility Allowance (BUA)-countable septic tank installation or maintenance expense that is the household's responsibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has BUA utility initial installation fee
Fact.Description: Whether the household has at least one Basic Utility Allowance (BUA)-countable initial utility installation fee that is the household's responsibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Non-heating utility allowance count
Fact.Description: The number of distinct household non-heating and non-cooling utility cost categories that can count toward the Basic Utility Allowance (BUA): electricity; water; sewer; trash; cooking fuel; telephone (landline, cellular, disposable cell phone, and VOIP grouped as one category); supplemental heating sources (space heater, electric blanket, heat lamp, and cooking stove used for heat grouped as one category); and infrastructure maintenance or installation costs that are the household's responsibility (well installation or maintenance, septic tank installation or maintenance, and utility initial installation fees each counted distinctly). Multiple expenses in the same category count only once (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Basic Utility Allowance minimum utility category count
Fact.Description: The minimum number of distinct non-heating or non-cooling utility cost categories a household must incur to qualify for the Basic Utility Allowance (BUA): at least two (2) categories (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has Basic Utility Allowance
Fact.Description: Whether the household incurs at least two non-heating or non-cooling utility costs, such as electricity, water, sewer, trash, cooking fuel, or telephone, satisfying the expense-count criterion for the Basic Utility Allowance (BUA). HCUA priority over BUA is handled by the utility allowance category selection (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has telephone utility allowance
Fact.Description: Whether the household is entitled to the telephone allowance because its only utility cost category is telephone service. If more than one SNAP household shares in paying telephone costs and telephone is the only utility cost of the dwelling, each SNAP household sharing the telephone costs receives the full phone standard (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Telephone utility allowance
Fact.Description: The full telephone standard allowed to a household whose only utility cost is telephone service. Effective October 1, 2025, the telephone standard is $97 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Has One Utility Allowance
Fact.Description: Whether the household is responsible for exactly one non-heating or non-cooling utility expense category, making it eligible for the One Utility Allowance (OUA) when it is not entitled to the HCUA, BUA, or telephone allowance. OUA priority after the telephone-only allowance is handled by the utility allowance category selection (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: One Utility Allowance
Fact.Description: The fixed One Utility Allowance (OUA) standard, also described as the fixed deduction for households whose only utility expense is something other than telephone, applied to households that are not entitled to the HCUA or BUA but are responsible for only one non-heating or one non-cooling utility expense other than telephone. If more than one SNAP household shares in paying one non-heating or non-cooling utility cost of the dwelling, each sharing household receives the full OUA. Effective October 1, 2025, the OUA standard is $71 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1; 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Utility cost
Fact.Description: The household's utility-cost amount for shelter budgeting, selected from the applicable standard utility allowance rather than actual utility expenses, including the telephone standard when telephone service is the household's only utility cost category (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Receives LEAP in last 12 months
Fact.Description: Whether the household received a Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) payment within the previous twelve (12) month period, which qualifies the household for the Heating and Cooling Utility Allowance (HCUA) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Receives BCE-qualifying benefits
Fact.Description: Whether this member receives, or is authorized to receive, SSI, Colorado Works (CW), Old Age Pension (OAP), Aid to the Needy Disabled (AND), or Aid to the Blind (AB). OAP, AND, and AB are captured under the Adult Financial cash grant (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Receives Family Preservation services
Fact.Description: Whether this member receives services from the Family Preservation Program. This determination must be documented in the case record (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: All members receive BCE-qualifying benefits
Fact.Description: Whether every household member receives, or is authorized to receive, SSI, Colorado Works (CW), Old Age Pension (OAP), Aid to the Needy Disabled (AND), Aid to the Blind (AB), or a combination of these benefits. The CW, SSI, OAP, and/or AB program(s) need only to authorize benefits for the household to be considered for BCE. Clients who are authorized to receive a benefit from one or more of these programs, but who are not paid such benefits because the grant is less than a minimum benefit or the benefits are suspended or are being recouped, are still considered eligible. Households entitled to Medicaid only are not considered SSI or Title IV-A participants (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Has member receiving Family Preservation services
Fact.Description: Whether at least one member who is part of the household receives services from the Family Preservation Program. This determination must be documented in the case record (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Disqualified for Basic Categorical Eligibility
Fact.Description: Whether the household is disqualified from being considered under Basic Categorical Eligibility (BCE) because any member is disqualified for a SNAP IPV or has been convicted of a drug-related felony where SNAP benefits were used to purchase drugs (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Has Basic Categorical Eligibility
Fact.Description: Whether the household qualifies for Basic Categorical Eligibility (BCE): either all members receive (or are authorized to receive) SSI, Colorado Works, Old Age Pension, Aid to the Needy Disabled, or Aid to the Blind, or at least one member receives services from the Family Preservation Program. A household cannot be considered under BCE if any member is disqualified for a SNAP IPV or has been convicted of a drug-related felony where SNAP benefits were used to purchase drugs; if the household received substantial lottery or gambling winnings during the month; or if the household previously lost eligibility due to substantial lottery or gambling winnings and must be considered under Standard Eligibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: ECE gross income rate
Fact.Description: The percentage of the federal poverty level used as the gross income threshold for Expanded Categorical Eligibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: ECE gross income threshold
Fact.Description: Two hundred percent (200%) of the federal poverty level for the household's size, below which a household's combined gross income must fall to qualify for Expanded Categorical Eligibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Receives non-cash TANF or MOE service
