Fact.Description: Whether the household has been authorized to receive a non-cash Temporary Assistance to Needy Families/Maintenance of Effort (TANF/MOE) funded service designed to further TANF Purpose Four (4) by "encouraging the formation and maintenance of two-parent families." Authorization is granted to households with combined gross income below two hundred percent (200%) of the federal poverty level (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Disqualified for Expanded Categorical Eligibility
Fact.Description: Whether the household is disqualified from being considered under Expanded Categorical Eligibility (ECE) because, at the time of application, any member is disqualified for a SNAP IPV or has been convicted of a drug-related felony where SNAP benefits were used to purchase drugs (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Has Expanded Categorical Eligibility
Fact.Description: Whether the household qualifies for Expanded Categorical Eligibility (ECE): the household has been authorized to receive a non-cash TANF/MOE funded service designed to further TANF Purpose Four (encouraging the formation and maintenance of two-parent families), which is granted to households with combined gross income below two hundred percent (200%) of the federal poverty level. A household cannot be considered under ECE if any member is disqualified for a SNAP IPV or has been convicted of a drug-related felony where SNAP benefits were used to purchase drugs; if the household received substantial lottery or gambling winnings during the month; or if the household previously lost eligibility due to substantial lottery or gambling winnings and must be considered under Standard Eligibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Standard Eligibility applies
Fact.Description: Whether Standard Eligibility (SE) rules shall be applied to the household. SE rules apply to households that include a member serving a disqualification for an IPV or fraud conviction; households that include a member convicted of a drug-related felony where SNAP benefits were used to purchase drugs; households that previously lost SNAP eligibility due to substantial lottery or gambling winnings and are reapplying after losing eligibility; or households that do not meet the criteria to be considered under BCE or ECE rules (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Elderly age minimum
Fact.Description: Lower bound (inclusive) of the age range for being considered "aged sixty (60) and older" under SNAP (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is elderly
Fact.Description: Whether this member is aged sixty (60) or older (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is elderly or person with disabilities
Fact.Description: Whether this member is aged sixty (60) or older, or is a person with a disability (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Is eligible for excess medical deduction
Fact.Description: Whether this member's medical expenses may be claimed for the excess medical deduction because the member is aged sixty (60) or older or is a person with disabilities; other household members, including spouses and dependents, cannot claim costs of their medical treatment and services for this deduction (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.6).

Fact.Name: Has member elderly or person with disabilities
Fact.Description: Whether the household includes a member aged sixty (60) or older or a person with a disability (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Gross income test rate
Fact.Description: The percentage of the federal poverty level used as the gross income threshold for Standard Eligibility households that do not include a member aged sixty (60) or older or a person with a disability (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Gross income threshold
Fact.Description: One hundred thirty percent (130%) of the federal poverty level for the household's size, at or below which the combined gross income of an SE household without a member aged sixty (60) or older or a person with a disability must fall (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Meets gross income test
Fact.Description: Whether the household's combined gross income is at or below one hundred thirty percent (130%) of the federal poverty level for the household's size (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Non-liquid resources
Fact.Description: The sum of non-liquid resources across all household members (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Resources
Fact.Description: The household's total countable resources, the sum of each member's total resources (liquid plus non-liquid) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Resource limit for households with elderly or disabled member
Fact.Description: The maximum allowable countable resources for a household that includes a member aged sixty (60) or older and/or a person with a disability, effective October 1, 2024 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.408).

Fact.Name: Normal resource limit
Fact.Description: The maximum allowable countable resources for a household that does not include a member aged sixty (60) or older and/or a person with a disability, effective October 1, 2024 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.408).

Fact.Name: Resource limit
Fact.Description: The maximum allowable countable resources for a household reviewed under Standard Eligibility rules: four thousand five hundred dollars ($4,500) if the household includes a member aged sixty (60) or older and/or a person with a disability, otherwise three thousand dollars ($3,000), effective October 1, 2024 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.408).

Fact.Name: Meets resource test
Fact.Description: Whether the household's countable resources are below the limit prescribed in Section 4.408 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Meets income criteria
Fact.Description: Whether the household meets the income criteria for Standard Eligibility: net income (after all applicable deductions) at or below one hundred percent (100%) of the federal poverty level; households that do not include a member aged sixty (60) or older or a person with a disability must additionally have combined gross income at or below one hundred thirty percent (130%) of the federal poverty level (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.401).

Fact.Name: Meets resource criteria
Fact.Description: Whether the household meets the resource criteria for Standard Eligibility, currently represented by the household meeting the resource test.

Fact.Name: Meets financial criteria
Fact.Description: Whether the household meets the financial criteria for Standard Eligibility by meeting both the income criteria and the resource criteria (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Has Standard Eligibility
Fact.Description: Whether the household qualifies under Standard Eligibility (SE): SE rules apply to the household, the household meets the SE financial criteria, and the household meets the nonfinancial eligibility criteria set out in Section 4.300. The household is also disqualified for the month if it received substantial lottery or gambling winnings during that month (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Eligibility category options
Fact.Description: The categories under which a household may be determined eligible for SNAP: Basic Categorical Eligibility (Bce), Expanded Categorical Eligibility (Ece), or Standard Eligibility (Se); Ineligible indicates the household does not qualify under any category (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Eligibility category
Fact.Description: The category of eligibility under which the household is determined eligible for SNAP: Basic Categorical Eligibility (BCE), Expanded Categorical Eligibility (ECE), or Standard Eligibility (SE); Ineligible if the household does not qualify under any category (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206)

Fact.Name: Extended certification period
Fact.Description: The twenty-four (24) month certification period assigned to households that contain only members aged sixty (60) and older and/or with a disability and have no earned income at the time of certification (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.208.1).

Fact.Name: Standard certification period
Fact.Description: The six (6) month certification period assigned to households that are not assigned the twenty-four (24) month certification period (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.208.1).

Fact.Name: Certification period
Fact.Description: The length, in months, of the period of time for which a household has been certified to receive benefits. A twenty-four (24) month certification period is assigned to households that contain only members aged sixty (60) and older and/or with a disability and have no earned income at the time of certification; all other households are assigned a six (6) month certification period (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.208.1).

Fact.Name: Countable months
Fact.Description: The number of countable months accrued by this member within the past 36 months. A countable month is a month in which an ABAWD received a full SNAP allotment but did not meet work requirements or have an exemption from those requirements. ABAWDs who accrue three countable months within a 36-month period become disqualified from SNAP unless they meet an exemption or ABAWD work requirements (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: D-SNAP active
Fact.Description: Whether the Disaster Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (D-SNAP) is active for the affected county, following a Presidential disaster declaration for individual assistance and at the county's discretion in coordination with the state SNAP office and FNS (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Temporary emergency active
Fact.Description: Whether a temporary emergency is active — an emergency caused by any natural or human-caused disaster, other than a major disaster declared by the President of the United States under the Disaster Relief Act of 1974, which is determined by FNS to have disrupted commercial channels of food distribution (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Disqualified for IPV/fraud
Fact.Description: Whether this member has been disqualified for an Intentional Program Violation/fraud (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Convicted of drug-related felony involving SNAP
Fact.Description: Whether this member has been convicted of a drug-related felony where SNAP benefits were used to purchase drugs. Drug-related felony has the same meaning as in 7 C.F.R. 273.11(m) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Failed to provide or obtain SSN
Fact.Description: Whether this member has failed to provide or obtain a Social Security Number (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is ineligible non-citizen
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an ineligible non-citizen. Citizens and non-citizen nationals are potentially eligible for SNAP; other non-citizens are ineligible unless they are a qualified non-citizen who is exempt from the additional-condition requirement, a qualified non-citizen who meets one of the additional conditions, or fall in one of the classes of non-qualified non-citizens eligible for participation (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305).

Fact.Name: Student ineligibility minimum age
Fact.Description: Lower bound (inclusive) of the age range subject to the SNAP student-eligibility rule. Persons aged seventeen (17) or under are not considered under student eligibility criteria (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306, B, 1).

Fact.Name: Student ineligibility maximum age
Fact.Description: Upper bound (inclusive) of the age range subject to the SNAP student-eligibility rule. Persons aged fifty (50) or over are not considered under student eligibility criteria (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306, B, 2).

Fact.Name: Student exemption work hours per week
Fact.Description: Minimum (inclusive) average hours worked per week for the SNAP student-eligibility employment exemption: twenty (20) hours per week. For non-self-employment, the student must be paid for the employment regardless of wages received; for self-employment, earnings after allowable business expenses are deducted must equal at least the federal minimum wage multiplied by twenty (20) hours (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, B).

Fact.Name: Student exemption dependent member age limit
Fact.Description: Upper bound (exclusive) on the age of a dependent household member whose care qualifies a full-time student for the SNAP student-eligibility exemption: a dependent household member under the age of six (6) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Student exemption dependent child age limit (single-parent provision)
Fact.Description: Upper bound (exclusive) on the age of a dependent child whose care qualifies a full-time, single-parent student for the SNAP student-eligibility exemption: a dependent child under age twelve (12) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Enrolled at least half time in an institution of higher education
Fact.Description: Whether this member is enrolled at least half time in an institution of higher education. Persons enrolled less than half time, persons enrolled full time in schools or training programs that are not institutions of higher education, persons attending high school, and persons participating in an on-the-job training program (training in an employment environment, excluding internships, field work, or practical experience associated with a course of higher education) are not considered under student eligibility criteria (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306, B, 3-6). Enrollment status begins on the first day of the school term of the institution of higher education and continues through normal periods of class attendance, vacation, and recess unless the student graduates, is suspended or expelled, drops out, or does not intend to register for the next normal school term (excluding summer session); for eligibility purposes enrollment starts when the student starts classes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306, C).

Fact.Name: Meets student eligibility exemption
Fact.Description: Whether this member meets at least one of the eight student-eligibility exemption criteria at 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1: A physically or mentally unfit for employment; B employed for an average of twenty (20) hours per week and paid for such employment; C participating in a state or federally financed work-study program; D responsible for the care of a dependent household member under age six (6), or a full-time student who is a single parent with responsibility for the care of a dependent child under age twelve (12) (the single-parent provision); E responsible for more than half of the physical care of a dependent household member aged six (6) to under twelve (12) where the local office has determined that adequate childcare is not available; F receiving a Title IV-A TANF cash grant; G assigned to or placed in an institution of higher education through a WIOA, Employment First, Trade Act, other state/local employment-and-training, or JOBS program; H participating in an on-the-job training program.

Fact.Name: Meets student employment exemption
Fact.Description: Whether this member meets the SNAP student-eligibility employment exemption through average employment of twenty (20) or more hours per week and paid for that employment, with self-employment additionally requiring earnings after allowable business expenses equal to at least the federal minimum wage multiplied by twenty (20) hours. Hours are added across the member's jobs in the applicable category (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, B).

Fact.Name: Student non-self-employment job hours per week
Fact.Description: The total average hours per week this member works across jobs that are not self-employment. These paid employment hours count toward the twenty (20) hour SNAP student-eligibility employment exemption regardless of wages received (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, B).

Fact.Name: Student self-employment federal-minimum-wage job hours per week
Fact.Description: The total average hours per week this member works across self-employment jobs whose earnings after allowable business expenses are deducted are at least equal to the federal minimum wage for the hours worked. These hours count toward the self-employment branch of the twenty (20) hour SNAP student-eligibility employment exemption (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, B).

Fact.Name: Is participating in work-study
Fact.Description: Whether this member is participating in a work-study program for purposes of the SNAP student eligibility exemption. The work-study shall be approved for the school term and the student shall anticipate working during that time. The student qualifies for this exemption the month the school term in which the work-study will occur begins or the month work-study is approved, whichever is later. The exemption continues until the end of the school term or until it becomes known that the student has refused an assignment. The exemption shall not continue between terms when there is a break of one (1) full month or longer unless the student is participating in work-study during the break (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Is assigned to higher education through an employment and training program
Fact.Description: Whether this member qualifies for the SNAP student eligibility exemption as a student assigned to or placed in an institution of higher education through a program under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA), Employment First (EF), a program under Section 236 of the Trade Act of 1974 (19 U.S.C. 2296), another program for the purpose of employment and training operated by the state or local government (program shall have at least one (1) component equivalent to the SNAP EF Program), or as a result of participating in the JOBS program under Title IV of the Social Security Act (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, G).

Fact.Name: Is full-time student
Fact.Description: Whether this member's /members/*/studentEnrollmentStatus is FullTime (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Has care of a dependent household member
Fact.Description: Whether this member has at least one /caregiverRelationships entry where the caregiver-side member provides more than half of the dependent-side member's physical care, and the dependent-side member is under the age of six (6). This captures responsibility for the care of a dependent household member under age six for the SNAP full-time-student exemption without prechecking the dependent's household membership, which follows from the caregiver relationship when the student is in the SNAP household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Is only household parent of a dependent child
Fact.Description: Whether this member has at least one parent-type /caregiverRelationships entry to a child under age twelve (12) where exactly one natural, adoptive, or stepparent relationship for that child is in the same SNAP household. Captures the parent branch of the single-parent full-time-student exemption without prechecking the child's household membership, which follows from the parent relationship when the student-parent is in the SNAP household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Has non-parent parental control of a dependent child without household parent or spouse
Fact.Description: Whether this member has at least one non-parent parental-control /caregiverRelationships entry to a child under age twelve (12), exactly one natural/adoptive/stepparent relationship for that child is in the SNAP household, and the member does not reside with their spouse. Captures the parental-control branch of the single-parent full-time-student exemption without prechecking the child's household membership (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Is single parent of a dependent child
Fact.Description: Whether this member satisfies either branch of the SNAP single-parent full-time-student exemption for a dependent household child under age twelve (12): the member is the child's only natural/adoptive/stepparent in the SNAP household, or the member has non-parent parental control while no natural/adoptive/stepparent is in the SNAP household and the member does not reside with their spouse (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Is student responsible for a dependent child
Fact.Description: Whether this member qualifies for the SNAP student eligibility exemption as a student who has responsibility for the care of a dependent household member under the age of six (6); or as a full-time student who is a single parent with responsibility for the care of a dependent child under age twelve (12). The full-time requirement only applies to the single-parent leg; the under-six leg applies to any student. The single-parent provision requires either exactly one natural/adoptive/stepparent relationship for the child in the SNAP household, or a non-parent parental-control relationship where no parent relationship is in the SNAP household and the student does not reside with their spouse (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Is student responsible for physical care of a dependent child without adequate childcare
Fact.Description: Whether this member qualifies for the SNAP student eligibility exemption as a student who is responsible for more than half of the physical care of a dependent household member who has reached the age of six (6) but is under the age of twelve (12), where the local office has determined that adequate childcare is not available to enable the individual to attend class and satisfy the requirement of item B or item C of 4.306.1. Derived from any /caregiverRelationships entry where this member is the caregiver, the dependent child is part of the SNAP household and aged six (6) to under twelve (12), and both per-relationship flags caregiverProvidesMoreThanHalfOfPhysicalCare and adequateChildcareUnavailable are true (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1, E).

Fact.Name: Is in K-12
Fact.Description: Whether this member is attending a K-12 school (kindergarten through twelfth grade). Persons attending high school are not considered under SNAP student eligibility criteria (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306, B, 5).

Fact.Name: Is ineligible student
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an ineligible student. A person aged eighteen (18) through forty-nine (49) and enrolled at least half time in an institution of higher education is ineligible to participate in the SNAP unless they meet one of the exemption criteria outlined at 4.306.1. Persons attending K-12 and persons participating in an on-the-job training program are not considered under student eligibility criteria (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306, B, 5-6).

Fact.Name: Disqualified for failure to cooperate with work requirements
Fact.Description: Whether this member has been disqualified for failure to cooperate with work requirements (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Voluntarily quit or reduced work effort
Fact.Description: Whether this member has voluntarily quit a job or reduced their work effort to less than 30 hours a week. Whether the quit or reduction was with good cause is captured separately on /members/*/voluntaryQuitReason (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1; 4.308).

Fact.Name: Voluntary quit reason options
Fact.Description: Options enumerating the reasons a member may give for a voluntary quit of employment or reduction in work hours. Most listed options are good-cause reasons not subject to sanction under SNAP: discrimination by an employer; work demands or conditions that render continued employment unreasonable; acceptance of new employment or at-least-half-time enrollment in a recognized school, training program, or institution of higher education that requires leaving employment; another household member accepting employment or at-least-half-time enrollment in another county or political sub-division that requires the household to move; resignations by persons under sixty (60) recognized by the employer as retirement; resignation from employment that does not meet the suitable-employment criteria of 4.310.7; circumstances beyond the individual's control where accepted full-time employment did not materialize or resulted in less than thirty (30) hours per week or weekly earnings below the federal minimum wage times thirty (30); leaving a job in connection with patterns of employment in which workers frequently move from one employer to another (such as migrant farm labor or construction work); illness of the head of household; illness of another household member requiring the head of household's presence; a household emergency; the unavailability of transportation; an employer demanding a reduction in the participant's work effort or salary through no fault of the employee; and lack of adequate child care for children who have reached age six (6) but are under age twelve (12). Other and StrikingGovernmentEmployee are not good-cause reasons; a federal, state, or local government employee dismissed for participating in a strike against that government is considered to have voluntarily quit without good cause (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.308.1).

Fact.Name: Voluntary quit reason
Fact.Description: The reason for this member's voluntary quit of employment or reduction in work hours from the list enumerated in /voluntaryQuitReasonOptions. Selecting one of the 4.308.1 enumerated good-cause reasons indicates good cause; selecting Other or StrikingGovernmentEmployee indicates there is no good cause and — combined with /members/*/voluntarilyQuitOrReducedWorkEffort — drives the ineligible-voluntary-quit determination (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.308.1).

Fact.Name: Is ineligible due to voluntary quit
Fact.Description: Whether this member is ineligible for SNAP participation because they voluntarily quit their most recent job or reduced their work effort below thirty (30) hours per week without good cause. True when /members/*/voluntarilyQuitOrReducedWorkEffort is true and /members/*/voluntaryQuitReason is set to Other (a reason was given but it does not fall within one of the enumerated 4.308.1 good-cause categories) or StrikingGovernmentEmployee (a federal, state, or local government employee dismissed for participating in a strike against that government is considered to have voluntarily quit without good cause) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.308; 4.308.1).

Fact.Name: Registered for work
Fact.Description: Whether this non-exempt member registered for work at initial application and at every recertification by signing the application for assistance or recertification, either personally or through an authorized representative or another adult household member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Provided employment status or availability information
Fact.Description: Whether this non-exempt member provided the eligibility technician sufficient information regarding employment status or availability for work (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Accepted suitable employment offer
Fact.Description: Whether this non-exempt member accepted an offer of employment that is suitable under the 4.310.7 criteria captured on /jobs/*/employmentIsSuitable (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310; 4.310.7).

Fact.Name: Reported to referred suitable employer
Fact.Description: Whether this non-exempt member reported to an employer when referred by the local office and the potential employment was suitable employment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Meets general work requirements
Fact.Description: Whether this member satisfies the SNAP general work requirements either by meeting a general work requirement exemption or, if non-exempt, by registering for work at application and recertification, providing sufficient information about employment status or availability for work, not committing an act of voluntary quit, accepting suitable employment, and reporting to a referred suitable employer when the potential employment is suitable (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Work-requirements always-exempt age maximum
Fact.Description: Upper bound (inclusive) for the SNAP general work requirement exemption for a person age fifteen (15) or younger (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Work-requirements conditional-minor age minimum
Fact.Description: Lower bound (inclusive) for the SNAP general work requirement exemption for a person age sixteen (16) or seventeen (17) who is not the head of household, is attending school, or is enrolled in an Employment and Training Program on at least a half-time basis (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Work-requirements conditional-minor age maximum
Fact.Description: Upper bound (inclusive) for the SNAP general work requirement exemption for a person age sixteen (16) or seventeen (17) who is not the head of household, is attending school, or is enrolled in an Employment and Training Program on at least a half-time basis (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Exempt from work requirements due to age
Fact.Description: Whether this member is exempt from SNAP general work requirements because they are age fifteen (15) or younger, age sixty (60) or older, or age sixteen (16) or seventeen (17) and either not the head of household, attending school, or enrolled in an Employment and Training Program on at least a half-time basis (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Applying for or receiving unemployment insurance benefits
Fact.Description: Whether this member is applying for or receiving Unemployment Insurance Benefits (UIB), including a person denied UIB who is appealing the decision, for purposes of the SNAP general work requirement exemption (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Regular participant in drug or alcohol treatment
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a regular participant in a drug or alcohol treatment or rehabilitation program for purposes of the SNAP general work requirement exemption (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Complying with Colorado Works or refugee services work program
Fact.Description: Whether this member is subject to and complying with Colorado Works (CW) or the Colorado Refugee Services Program (CRSP) work programs for purposes of the SNAP general work requirement exemption (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Meets general work requirement exception
Fact.Description: Whether this member meets a SNAP general work requirement exemption: qualifying age, responsibility for the care of a dependent child under six (6) or incapacitated person, physical or mental unfitness for employment, at-least-half-time student enrollment, qualifying employment or self-employment, applying for or receiving UIB, regular participation in drug or alcohol treatment or rehabilitation, or complying with CW or CRSP work programs (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Exempt from work requirements due to caregiving
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a parent or other household member responsible for the care of a dependent child under six (6) or an incapacitated person, based on a claimed /caregiverRelationships entry for this caregiver. The dependent-side member does not need to be part of the SNAP household. The claimed relationship selects the single caregiver who receives the exemption when multiple caregivers are listed for the same dependent (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Work-requirements care exemption dependent child age limit
Fact.Description: Upper bound (exclusive) on the age of a dependent child whose care can qualify one parent or other household member for the SNAP work-requirements exemption: a dependent child under age six (6) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Exempt from work requirements due to student enrollment
Fact.Description: Whether this member is exempt from SNAP work requirements because they are enrolled at least half-time, as defined by the educational facility, in an accredited school, training program, or institution of higher education. Students who are eligible for SNAP remain exempt during normal periods of class attendance and school breaks; persons enrolled less than half-time, or with an enrollment-status break due to graduation, expulsion, suspension, dropping out, or not intending to register for the next normal school term other than summer, do not qualify for this exemption. A student enrolled in an institution of higher education must also meet SNAP student-eligibility requirements to receive SNAP (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Work-requirements employment exemption hours per week
Fact.Description: Minimum hours per week for the SNAP work-requirement employment exemption: employed or self-employed individuals qualify when working at least thirty (30) hours per week or when receiving weekly earnings at least equal to the federal minimum wage multiplied by thirty (30) hours (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Work-requirements employment exemption monthly earnings limit
Fact.Description: Monthly earnings threshold for the SNAP work-requirement employment exemption, equal to the federal minimum wage hourly rate multiplied by thirty (30) hours and the weekly-to-monthly conversion multiplier (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Exempt from work requirements due to employment
Fact.Description: Whether this member is exempt from SNAP work requirements because the member is employed or self-employed for a total of thirty (30) or more hours per week, or has non-exempt earned income at least equal to the federal minimum wage multiplied by thirty (30) hours and converted to a monthly amount (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Work-requirements total job hours per week
Fact.Description: The total average hours per week this member works across employed or self-employed jobs that are paid at least the federal minimum wage. A total of at least thirty (30) such hours per week can qualify the member for the SNAP work-requirement employment exemption (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Disqualified for failure to cooperate with QA division
Fact.Description: Whether this member has been disqualified for failure to cooperate with the state quality assurance division (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Physically or mentally unfit for employment for student eligibility
Fact.Description: Whether this member is physically or mentally unfit for employment for purposes of the SNAP student eligibility exemption. This student-specific flag is separate from the work-requirements unfitness determination so the two policy contexts can be captured independently (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.306.1).

Fact.Name: Physically or mentally unfit for employment for work requirements
Fact.Description: Whether this member is physically or mentally unfit for employment for purposes of SNAP work requirements. Examples include persons experiencing homelessness, persons recently released from an institution, persons with disabilities including self-declared temporary conditions preventing successful participation in work activities, persons receiving temporary or permanent disability benefits from government or private sources, persons participating in vocational rehabilitation, persons applying for or appealing SSI benefits, persons unable to maintain employment, and persons impacted by domestic violence (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Recently released from an institution
Fact.Description: Whether this member was recently released from an institution, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Has self-declared temporary condition preventing work activities
Fact.Description: Whether this member has a self-declared temporary condition that would prevent successful participation in work activities, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Receives temporary or permanent disability benefits
Fact.Description: Whether this member receives temporary or permanent disability benefits issued by government or private sources, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Is participating in vocational rehabilitation
Fact.Description: Whether this member is participating in vocational rehabilitation, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Is applying for or appealing SSI benefits
Fact.Description: Whether this member is applying for and/or appealing Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Is work-requirement disabled
Fact.Description: Whether this member meets the disability-related examples of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes: a person with disabilities as defined in 4.100, including but not limited to self-declared temporary conditions that would prevent successful participation in work activities, receipt of temporary or permanent disability benefits issued by government or private sources, participation in vocational rehabilitation, or applying for and/or appealing SSI benefits (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Is unable to maintain employment
Fact.Description: Whether this member is unable to maintain employment, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Is impacted by domestic violence
Fact.Description: Whether this member is impacted by domestic violence, which is an example of being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Has other valid reason for work-requirements unfitness
Fact.Description: Whether this member has another valid reason, not otherwise listed, for being physically or mentally unfit for employment for SNAP work-requirements purposes. The listed examples of unfitness are not exhaustive (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.310).

Fact.Name: Enrolled in Employment and Training Program
Fact.Description: Whether this member is enrolled in the Employment and Training Program (Employment First/EF), a program operated by the Department of Human Services consisting of work, training, education, work experience, and/or job search activities designed to help clients obtain gainful employment (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: In on-the-job training
Fact.Description: Whether this member has any job marked as on-the-job training (OJT), meaning training provided to an employee after they are hired and designed for individuals who do not have the necessary work experience required for the job (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Is already participating in another household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is already receiving SNAP benefits as part of another SNAP household or in another state in the same calendar month (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Resident of a shelter for battered women and children
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a resident of a public or private nonprofit residential facility that serves battered women and their children (10 CCR 2506-1)

Fact.Name: Disqualified for participating in another household
Fact.Description: Whether this member is disqualified because they are already participating in another SNAP household in the same month. Residents of a shelter for battered women and children are exempt from this restriction (10 CCR 2506-1)

Fact.Name: Disqualified for felony conviction non-compliance
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a person with a felony conviction who is not in compliance with the terms of their sentence and was convicted as an adult for conduct that occurred after February 7, 2014 for any of the following crimes: aggravated sexual abuse under Section 2241 of Title 18, United States Code; murder under Section 1111 of Title 18, United States Code; an offense under Chapter 110 of Title 18, United States Code; a federal or state offense involving sexual assault, as defined in Section 40002(a) of the Violence Against Women Act of 1994 (42 U.S.C. 13925(a)); or an offense under state law determined by the attorney general to be substantially similar to the foregoing (10 CCR 2506-1)

Fact.Name: Disqualified for living in a boarding house or institution
Fact.Description: Whether this member is disqualified because they are a resident of a commercial or noncommercial boarding house or an institution that has not been authorized by FNS to accept SNAP benefits, and they do not qualify for an exemption under Section 4.304.41 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.4)

Fact.Name: Disqualified for parole or probation violation
Fact.Description: Whether this member is disqualified as a parole or probation violator. An impartial party designated by the agency must determine that the individual violated a condition of probation or parole imposed under federal or state law, and that federal, state, or local law enforcement authorities are actively seeking the individual to enforce those conditions. Active pursuit is established when a law enforcement agency informs the local office it intends to enforce an outstanding felony warrant or arrest the individual for a probation or parole violation within 20 days of submitting a request for information about the individual; presents a felony arrest warrant as provided in 4.304.4, B, 1; or states it intends to enforce an outstanding felony warrant or arrest the individual for a probation or parole violation within 30 days of the date of a request from a local office about a specific outstanding felony warrant or probation or parole violation (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.4)

Fact.Name: Is pregnant
Fact.Description: Whether this member is pregnant for purposes of the ABAWD exemption from the ABAWD work requirement (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.311.1).

Fact.Name: Is veteran
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a veteran for purposes of the ABAWD exemption from the ABAWD work requirement (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.311.1).

Fact.Name: Was in foster care on 18th birthday
Fact.Description: Whether this member was in foster care on their eighteenth (18th) birthday for purposes of the ABAWD exemption for individuals aged twenty-four (24) years and younger (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.311.1).

Fact.Name: Exempt under ABAWD waiver
Fact.Description: Whether this member is exempt from the ABAWD work requirement under a waiver approved by USDA FNS (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.311.1).

Fact.Name: Exempt under Colorado ABAWD state exemption
Fact.Description: Whether this member is exempt from the ABAWD work requirement using a Colorado-defined state exemption identified in the current SNAP Employment and Training State Plan (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.311.1).

Fact.Name: ABAWD foster care exemption maximum age
Fact.Description: Upper bound (inclusive) for the ABAWD exemption for individuals aged twenty-four (24) years and younger and in foster care on their eighteenth (18th) birthday (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.311.1).

Fact.Name: Young adult foster care ABAWD exempt
Fact.Description: Whether this member is aged twenty-four (24) years or younger and was in foster care on their eighteenth (18th) birthday for purposes of the ABAWD exemption from the ABAWD work requirement (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.311.1).

Fact.Name: Is ABAWD exempt
Fact.Description: Whether this member meets an ABAWD exemption from the ABAWD work requirement by being exempt from the general work requirements, pregnant, experiencing homelessness, a veteran, aged twenty-four (24) years or younger and in foster care on their eighteenth (18th) birthday, exempt under a USDA FNS waiver, or exempt under a Colorado-defined state exemption in the current SNAP Employment and Training State Plan (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.311.1).

Fact.Name: ABAWD countable months limit
Fact.Description: The number of countable months an ABAWD may accrue within a thirty-six (36) month window before being disqualified (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: ABAWD work requirement hours per week
Fact.Description: Minimum weekly hours needed to fulfill the ABAWD work requirement through work, a qualifying work program, or a combination of work and a qualifying work program: twenty (20) hours per week (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Average ABAWD work hours per week
Fact.Description: This member's average weekly ABAWD work hours from jobs classified as compensated work, in-kind work, or unpaid work verified by the provider of the unpaid work. This average is used for both the twenty (20) hours per week threshold and the eighty (80) hours per month averaged-monthly threshold (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: ABAWD work program hours per week
Fact.Description: This member's weekly hours participating in and complying with a qualifying ABAWD work program, including a CDHS-operated or supervised employment and training program other than job search or job-search training, a WIOA program, or a Trade Act Section 236 program (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Participates in Colorado Workfare
Fact.Description: Whether this member is participating in and complying with the Colorado Workfare program for purposes of fulfilling the ABAWD work requirement (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Meets ABAWD work requirement
Fact.Description: Whether this member fulfills the ABAWD work requirement by working at least twenty (20) average hours per week (including work averaged monthly), participating in and complying with a qualifying work program for at least twenty (20) average hours per week (including participation averaged monthly), combining work and qualifying work-program participation to reach that threshold, or participating in and complying with the Colorado Workfare program (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Is ABAWD not meeting work requirement or exemption
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an ABAWD who is not meeting the ABAWD work requirement and does not meet an ABAWD exemption from those requirements (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1; 4.311.1).

Fact.Name: Exceeded ABAWD countable months limit
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an ABAWD who has accrued at least the limit of countable months without meeting an exemption or ABAWD work requirements (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Has E-EBT in last 12 months
Fact.Description: Whether the household received an Energy Electronic Benefit Transfer (E-EBT) payment within the previous twelve (12) month period, which qualifies the household for the Heating and Cooling Utility Allowance (HCUA) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.31).

Fact.Name: Medical expense deduction minimum
Fact.Description: The first thirty-five dollars ($35) of verified monthly medical expenses that is not deductible before applying either the Standard Medical Expense Deduction (SMED) or actual excess medical expenses (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.61).

Fact.Name: Standard Medical Expense Deduction
Fact.Description: The Standard Medical Expense Deduction (SMED), used when total verified monthly medical expenses are greater than thirty-five dollars ($35) and the amount remaining after subtracting the first thirty-five dollars ($35) does not exceed the SMED. Effective amount modeled here is one hundred sixty-five dollars ($165) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.61).

Fact.Name: Allowable medical expenses
Fact.Description: The household's total monthly allowable medical expenses before subtracting the first thirty-five dollars ($35), including monthly amounts for expenses marked as allowable medical expenses (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.6; 4.407.61).

Fact.Name: Allowable medical expenses after minimum
Fact.Description: The household's total monthly allowable medical expenses after subtracting the first thirty-five dollars ($35), floored at zero (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.61).

Fact.Name: Excess medical deduction
Fact.Description: The household's monthly excess medical deduction. If allowable monthly medical expenses exceed thirty-five dollars ($35) but the amount remaining after subtracting the first thirty-five dollars ($35) is less than or equal to the Standard Medical Expense Deduction (SMED), the SMED is allowed; if the amount remaining after subtracting the first thirty-five dollars ($35) exceeds the SMED, actual excess medical expenses are allowed (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.61).

Fact.Name: Ineligible inclusion ratio
Fact.Description: The member-level inclusion ratio for income or expenses subject to ineligible non-citizen, missing-SSN, or ABAWD sanction proration. Members who are not ineligible non-citizens, have not failed to provide or obtain a Social Security Number, and are not sanctioned as ABAWDs who have received three months of SNAP benefits in a thirty-six month period are included in full. For a member who is an ineligible non-citizen, has failed to provide or obtain a Social Security Number, or is sanctioned as an ABAWD who has received three months of SNAP benefits in a thirty-six month period, the includable share is the number of household members who are not ineligible non-citizens, have not failed to provide or obtain a Social Security Number, and are not sanctioned as ABAWDs divided by the total number of members in the household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3, A).

Fact.Name: Allowable monthly shelter costs
Fact.Description: The household's allowable monthly shelter costs: the applicable standard utility allowance in full, plus non-utility shelter expenses paid or billed to eligible household members in full, and non-utility shelter expenses paid or billed to a person disqualified for being an ineligible non-citizen or for failure to provide a Social Security Number with all except that person's pro rata share counted (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3, A).

Fact.Name: Has or expects shelter costs
Fact.Description: Whether the household incurs, or reasonably expects to incur, shelter costs during the month. Households experiencing homelessness that incur no shelter costs during the month are not eligible for the homeless shelter deduction estimate (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3, C).

Fact.Name: Homeless shelter deduction estimate
Fact.Description: The standard estimate of shelter expenses available to households in which all individuals are experiencing homelessness and that incur, or reasonably expect to incur, shelter costs during the month. Effective October 1, 2025, the estimate is one hundred ninety-eight dollars and ninety-nine cents ($198.99) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3, C).

Fact.Name: All household members experiencing homelessness
Fact.Description: Whether all individuals in the SNAP household are experiencing homelessness, used to determine eligibility for the homeless shelter deduction estimate (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3, C).

Fact.Name: Monthly shelter costs for excess shelter deduction
Fact.Description: The monthly shelter-cost amount used for the excess shelter deduction. Households in which all individuals are experiencing homelessness and that incur, or reasonably expect to incur, shelter costs may use the standard homeless shelter estimate unless higher actual shelter costs are verified; otherwise the household's allowable monthly shelter costs are used (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3, C).

Fact.Name: Income after deductions before excess shelter deduction
Fact.Description: The household's monthly income after all currently modeled deductions other than the excess shelter deduction, used to determine the fifty percent (50%) shelter-cost threshold for the excess shelter deduction (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3, A).

Fact.Name: Excess shelter deduction income rate
Fact.Description: The fifty percent (50%) share of household income after all other deductions that allowable monthly shelter costs must exceed for the excess shelter deduction (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3, A).

Fact.Name: Excess shelter deduction cap
Fact.Description: The maximum excess shelter deduction for households that do not contain a person aged sixty (60) or older or a person with a disability. Effective October 1, 2025, the cap is seven hundred forty-four dollars ($744) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3, B).

Fact.Name: Uncapped excess shelter deduction
Fact.Description: The amount by which the household's monthly shelter costs for the excess shelter deduction exceed fifty percent (50%) of the household's income after all other currently modeled deductions, floored at zero and before applying the shelter deduction cap (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3).

Fact.Name: Excess shelter deduction
Fact.Description: The household's excess shelter deduction. Households containing a person aged sixty (60) or older or a person with a disability receive the full uncapped amount by which monthly shelter costs exceed fifty percent (50%) of income after all other deductions; other households are limited to the shelter deduction cap (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.3).

Fact.Name: Standard deduction
Fact.Description: The standard deduction allowed to all SNAP households, based on eligible household size and capped at the six-person amount for households with six (6) or more eligible members. Effective October 1, 2025, household sizes 1-3 receive $209, size 4 receives $223, size 5 receives $261, and size 6 or more receives $299 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.1).

Fact.Name: Standard deduction for 1-3 person household
Fact.Description: Standard deduction amount for SNAP households with one (1), two (2), or three (3) eligible members, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.1).

Fact.Name: Standard deduction for 4-person household
Fact.Description: Standard deduction amount for SNAP households with four (4) eligible members, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.1).

Fact.Name: Standard deduction for 5-person household
Fact.Description: Standard deduction amount for SNAP households with five (5) eligible members, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.1).

Fact.Name: Standard deduction for 6-or-more-person household
Fact.Description: Standard deduction amount for SNAP households with six (6) or more eligible members, effective October 1, 2025 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.1).

Fact.Name: Substantial lottery or gambling winnings threshold
Fact.Description: A cash prize won in a single game, before taxes or other amounts are withheld, that is equal to or greater than this threshold counts as substantial lottery or gambling winnings. The threshold equals the resource limit for persons aged sixty (60) and older and persons with disabilities (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1; 4.408).

Fact.Name: Has substantial lottery or gambling winnings this month
Fact.Description: Whether the household's largest single-game lottery or gambling cash prize during the month equals or exceeds the substantial lottery or gambling winnings threshold. Such winnings from an individual will disqualify the entire SNAP household from eligibility in the month the winnings are received (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Had previous substantial lottery or gambling winnings
Fact.Description: Whether the SNAP household previously lost eligibility because a member received substantial lottery or gambling winnings. The next time such a household reapplies and is certified for SNAP after losing eligibility, the household must be considered under Standard Eligibility (SE) guidelines; after receiving SNAP as an SE household, the household will be re-evaluated for categorical eligibility at the next eligible certification period (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.206).

Fact.Name: Non-exempt earned income
Fact.Description: This member's monthly earned income after any per-income exempt amount has been subtracted from each income entry before monthly conversion (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1; 4.403; 4.405).

Fact.Name: Earned income deduction eligible income
Fact.Description: This member's monthly gross nonexempt earned income eligible for the twenty percent (20%) earned income deduction, excluding any portion earned under a work supplementation or work support program that is attributable to a federal, state, or local public assistance program. For a member subject to ineligible inclusion proration, the earned income deduction applies only to the prorated income attributed to the household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.2; 4.407.3, A).

Fact.Name: Unearned income
Fact.Description: This member's unearned income (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1; 4.404), including monthly income entries whose source is treated as unearned income and this member's post-exemption sponsor income. SponsorPayments income entries are excluded from the direct income-entry sum because /members/*/sponsorIncome separately applies the sponsor deeming rules and actual-money-paid comparison.

Fact.Name: Unearned income (including sponsor income)
Fact.Description: This member's unearned income for the indigent-non-citizen determination (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, E, 4; 4.404). Mirrors /members/*/unearnedIncome but points at /members/*/deemedSponsorIncome — the raw per-non-citizen deemed share — instead of /members/*/sponsorIncome, so the indigence check uses sponsor income before the 4.000.1, E exemptions are applied and avoids cycling through /members/*/sponsorIncomeAndResourcesDoNotApply.

Fact.Name: Liquid resources
Fact.Description: The sum of this household member's countable liquid resource item values, including cash on hand, money in checking or savings accounts, saving certificates, stocks or bonds, and non-recurring lump sum payments specified in 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.405, F.

Fact.Name: Non-liquid resources
Fact.Description: The sum of this household member's countable non-liquid resource item values, such as personal effects, household goods, vehicles, buildings, land, and other real property (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1; 4.408.1).

Fact.Name: Resources
Fact.Description: This member's total countable resources, the sum of liquid resources, non-liquid resources, and any sponsor resources deemed to this member as a sponsored non-citizen (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Gross income
Fact.Description: The total of all non-exempt earned and unearned income after subtracting this member's legally obligated child support income exclusion, prorated by the member's ineligible inclusion ratio when the member is disqualified for being an ineligible non-citizen, for failure or refusal to obtain or provide a SSN, or as an ABAWD who has received three months of SNAP benefits in a thirty-six month period. Legally obligated child support is deducted before applying ineligible inclusion proration (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1; 4.405, D; 4.407.3, A).

Fact.Name: Gross income (including sponsor income)
Fact.Description: This member's gross income with /members/*/unearnedIncomeWithSponsorIncome standing in for /members/*/unearnedIncome — i.e., using /members/*/deemedSponsorIncome (the raw per-non-citizen deemed share, NOT the post-exemption /members/*/sponsorIncome) as the sponsor-income contribution. Used to assess indigent non-citizen status (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, E, 4) without cycling through /members/*/sponsorIncomeAndResourcesDoNotApply, since indigence itself feeds into that exemption umbrella.

Fact.Name: Net income test rate
Fact.Description: The percentage of the federal poverty level used as the net income test threshold (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Net income threshold
Fact.Description: One hundred percent (100%) of the federal poverty level for the household's size, under which a household's income must fall after all allowable deductions are considered (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Earned income deduction rate
Fact.Description: The percentage of gross nonexempt earned income deducted for households with earned income (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.2, A).

Fact.Name: Earned income deduction
Fact.Description: Twenty percent (20%) of the household's gross nonexempt earned income, excluding any income earned under a work supplementation or work support program that is attributable to a federal, state, or local public assistance program; zero when an Inadvertent Household Error (IHE) claim is due to earned income being reported in an untimely manner (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407.2; 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Deductions
Fact.Description: The household-wide total monthly allowable deductions subtracted from total monthly gross income to determine monthly net SNAP income (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407, A).

Fact.Name: Net income
Fact.Description: The household's monthly net SNAP income after subtracting household-wide allowable deductions from total monthly gross income, used for the net income test (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.407, A).

Fact.Name: Meets net income test
Fact.Description: Whether the household's net income falls at or below one hundred percent (100%) of the federal poverty level for the household's size (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Participates in Commodity Food Distribution Program
Fact.Description: Whether the household is on an Indian reservation and participating in the Commodity Food Distribution Program for the current period. Participation must be limited to either the Commodity Food Distribution Program or SNAP, not both (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.304.4).

Fact.Name: Lives in application county or district
Fact.Description: Whether the household lives in the county or district in which they make application for the Program (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.303).

Fact.Name: Has nearby county/district filing arrangement
Fact.Description: Whether the local office has made arrangements to allow this household to file an application in a nearby specified county/district office (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.303).

Fact.Name: Meets residency requirement
Fact.Description: Whether the household meets the residency requirement: applicants shall live in the county or district in which they make application for the Program, unless the local office has made arrangements to allow particular households to file an application in a nearby specified county/district office (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.303).

Fact.Name: Meets non-financial criteria
Fact.Description: Whether the household meets the set of rules other than those governing the household's gross and net income and resource standards (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Is experiencing homelessness
Fact.Description: Whether this member lacks a fixed and regular nighttime residence or whose primary residence is a supervised shelter designed for temporary accommodations; a halfway house or similar facility that provides temporary residence; a place not designed for or ordinarily used as regular sleeping accommodations for human beings; or a temporary accommodation in the residence of another individual for ninety (90) days or less (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is fleeing felon
Fact.Description: Whether this member is fleeing to avoid prosecution or custody for a crime, or an attempt to commit a crime, that would be classified as a felony under a state or federal law (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is migrant farm worker
Fact.Description: Whether this member travels away from home on a regular basis to follow the flow of seasonal agricultural work (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Is striker
Fact.Description: Whether this member is involved in a strike or other concerted stoppage of work by employees, including a stoppage by reason of the expiration of a collective bargaining agreement and any concerted slowdown or other concerted interruption of operations by employees (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1)

Fact.Name: Was eligible for SNAP the day before the strike
Fact.Description: Whether the household containing this striking member was eligible for SNAP the day before the strike. A household containing a striker is only eligible for SNAP if the household was eligible the day before the strike and is otherwise eligible at the time of the strike (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305).

Fact.Name: Was exempt from work registration the day before the strike
Fact.Description: Whether this striking member was exempt from work registration the day before the strike, such as the caretaker of a child under six (6) years of age, other than persons exempt solely on the ground that they were employed. Households where the striking member was so exempt are not subject to the striker eligibility restriction (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, A and D).

Fact.Name: Is ineligible striker
Fact.Description: Whether this member is an ineligible striker. A household containing a striking member shall not be eligible for SNAP unless the household was eligible for the Program the day before the strike and is otherwise eligible at the time of the strike. Households where the striking member was exempt from work registration the day before the strike (other than persons exempt solely on the ground that they were employed) are not subject to these provisions (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305).

Fact.Name: Student enrollment status options
Fact.Description: Options describing a member's enrollment status in an institution of higher education — an institution that normally requires a high school diploma or equivalency certificate for a student to enroll, such as a college, university, or vocational or technical school: full time (a school schedule equivalent to a full-time curriculum as defined by the institution of higher education the person is attending), at least half time but less than full time, or less than half time / not enrolled (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Student enrollment status
Fact.Description: This member's enrollment status in an institution of higher education — an institution that normally requires a high school diploma or equivalency certificate for a student to enroll, such as a college, university, or vocational or technical school: full time (a school schedule equivalent to a full-time curriculum as defined by the institution of higher education the person is attending), at least half time but less than full time, or less than half time / not enrolled (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Citizenship/immigration status options
Fact.Description: Options describing a member's citizenship or immigration status for SNAP citizenship and non-citizenship eligibility: U.S. citizen; non-citizen national; qualified non-citizen statuses including lawful permanent resident, parolee, asylee, refugee, withholding of deportation or removal, conditional entrant, Cuban or Haitian entrant, battered immigrant, victim of severe trafficking, Amerasian, or Iraqi/Afghan special immigrant; eligible non-qualified non-citizen statuses including American Indian born abroad or Hmong/Highland Laotian Tribal Member; and other non-citizen statuses (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305).

Fact.Name: Citizenship/immigration status
Fact.Description: This member's selected citizenship or immigration status for SNAP citizenship and non-citizenship eligibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305).

Fact.Name: Is qualified non-citizen without additional condition
Fact.Description: Whether this member is in a qualified non-citizen status that is eligible for SNAP participation indefinitely from the date the non-citizen obtains qualified non-citizen status or enters the U.S. in a qualifying status, without having to meet an additional condition: refugees admitted under 8 U.S.C. 1157, victims of trafficking under the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000, asylees granted asylum under Section 208 of the INA, non-citizens whose deportation or removal is being withheld under 8 U.S.C. 1224(H) or 8 U.S.C. 1231(B)(3), Cuban or Haitian entrants under 8 U.S.C. 1522(E), Amerasians under 8 U.S.C. 1612, and Iraqi or Afghan Special Immigrants under 8 U.S.C. 1101(A)(27) (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 2, a).

Fact.Name: Is qualified non-citizen with additional condition
Fact.Description: Whether this member is in a qualified non-citizen status that is required to meet an additional condition (see Section 4.305, B, 3) to be eligible for participation in the Program: Lawfully Admitted for Permanent Residence (LPRs) under the Immigration and Nationality Act, non-citizens paroled into the United States under 8 U.S.C. 1182(d)(5) for at least one (1) year, non-citizens granted conditional entry pursuant to 8 U.S.C. 1153(a)(7) as in effect before April 1, 1980, and non-citizens who have been battered or subjected to extreme cruelty in the U.S. by a family member with whom the non-citizen resides (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 2, b).

Fact.Name: Is qualified non-citizen
Fact.Description: Whether this member meets the definition of "qualified alien" under 7 C.F.R. 273.4(a)(5), (6)(1) (2019) for SNAP purposes: lawful permanent residents, asylees, refugees, parolees, individuals granted withholding of deportation or removal, conditional entrants, Cuban or Haitian entrants, battered immigrants, and non-citizen victims of a severe form of trafficking. This term is not itself an immigration status; qualified non-citizens are not automatically eligible for SNAP and must meet all other eligibility requirements (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B).

Fact.Name: Is eligible non-qualified non-citizen
Fact.Description: Whether this member is in a class of non-citizens that is not defined as a qualified non-citizen status but is potentially eligible for SNAP participation without having to meet an additional condition (see Section 4.305, B, 3): certain American Indians born abroad, and Hmong or Highland Laotian Tribal Members. All other classes of non-citizens that are not in a qualified status are not eligible for participation in SNAP (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 2).

Fact.Name: Non-citizen child age limit (additional-condition case)
Fact.Description: Upper bound (exclusive) on a non-citizen's age for the children-under-eighteen additional condition (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 3, c): a non-citizen under eighteen (18) years of age in a qualified non-citizen status who lawfully resides in the U.S. satisfies the additional-condition requirement. When the non-citizen turns eighteen (18), non-citizen eligibility shall be reviewed.

Fact.Name: Qualified non-citizen residence years threshold
Fact.Description: Lower bound (inclusive) on the number of years a non-citizen must have lived in the U.S. in a qualified non-citizen status to satisfy the five-year residence additional condition (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 3, a).

Fact.Name: Qualified years in the U.S.
Fact.Description: The number of years this non-citizen has lived in the U.S. in a qualified non-citizen status. The waiting period begins on the date the non-citizen obtains status as a qualified non-citizen or enters the U.S. in a qualifying status (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 3, a).

Fact.Name: Has five years in a qualified non-citizen status
Fact.Description: Whether this non-citizen has lived in the U.S. in a qualified non-citizen status for five (5) years. The five (5) year waiting period begins on the date the non-citizen obtains status as a qualified non-citizen or enters the U.S. in a qualifying status (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 3, a).

Fact.Name: Qualifying work quarters threshold
Fact.Description: Lower bound (inclusive) on the number of qualifying work quarters a non-citizen must have to satisfy the work-quarters additional condition (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 3, b).

Fact.Name: Qualifying work quarters
Fact.Description: The total number of qualifying work quarters credited to this non-citizen under Title II of the Social Security Act. The sum may include the non-citizen's own quarters, quarters credited from the work of a parent while the non-citizen was under eighteen (18), and quarters credited from the work of the non-citizen's spouse, subject to the restrictions in 4.305, B, 3, b (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 3, b).

Fact.Name: Has forty qualifying work quarters
Fact.Description: Whether this non-citizen has satisfied the forty (40) qualifying work quarters additional condition, as defined under Title II of the Social Security Act. The sum may include the non-citizen's own quarters, quarters credited from the work of a parent while the non-citizen was under eighteen (18), and quarters credited from the work of the non-citizen's spouse, subject to the restrictions in 4.305, B, 3, b (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 3, b).

Fact.Name: Born on or before August 22, 1931 and lawfully resided in the U.S. on August 22, 1996
Fact.Description: Whether this non-citizen was born on or before August 22, 1931 and lawfully resided in the U.S. on August 22, 1996 (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 3, e).

Fact.Name: Has qualifying military connection
Fact.Description: Whether this qualified non-citizen has a qualifying military connection: an individual lawfully residing in a state on active duty (other than training) in the military, excluding national guard; an honorably discharged veteran (as defined in Section 101 of Title 38, U.S.C.) whose discharge is not because of immigration status and who fulfills the minimum active-duty service requirements, including an individual who died in active military, naval, or air service; or the spouse, un-remarried surviving spouse, or unmarried dependent child of such a person, as further defined in 4.305, B, 3, f (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 3, f).

Fact.Name: Meets additional condition for non-citizen eligibility
Fact.Description: Whether this member, who is in a qualified non-citizen status as outlined in subsection 4.305, B, 1, satisfies at least one of the additional conditions listed in 4.305, B, 3, required for eligibility for participation in the Program: five (5) years of residence in a qualified non-citizen status, forty (40) qualifying work quarters, under eighteen (18) years of age, a person with disabilities, born on or before August 22, 1931 and lawfully residing in the U.S. on August 22, 1996, or a qualifying military connection (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B, 3).

Fact.Name: Is eligible non-citizen
Fact.Description: Whether this non-citizen member is eligible for SNAP participation: they are a qualified non-citizen who is either not required to meet an additional condition (4.305, B, 2, a) or meets one of the additional conditions in 4.305, B, 3, OR they fall in one of the classes of non-qualified non-citizens eligible for participation (4.305, B, 2). Each category stands alone for purposes of determining eligibility (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.305, B).

Fact.Name: Is sponsored non-citizen
Fact.Description: Whether this member is a non-citizen lawfully admitted for permanent residence into the United States who has been sponsored by an individual for entry into the country, derived from whether /members/*/sponsorId is set on this member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1).

Fact.Name: Sponsor earned income deduction rate
Fact.Description: The fraction of the sponsor and sponsor's spouse's earned income subtracted from their combined gross income when deeming sponsor income to a sponsored non-citizen. Twenty percent (20%) per 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 2, a.

Fact.Name: Sponsor and spouse gross income
Fact.Description: The combined gross income of this sponsored non-citizen's sponsor and the sponsor's spouse, used in sponsor income deeming (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D). The spouse's income is counted even if the sponsor and spouse were married after the signing of the affidavit of support.

Fact.Name: Sponsor and spouse non-exempt earned income
Fact.Description: The combined non-exempt earned income of this sponsored non-citizen's sponsor and the sponsor's spouse, used in the twenty percent (20%) earned-income reduction in sponsor income deeming (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 2, a).

Fact.Name: Sponsor and spouse dependent count
Fact.Description: The number of other people who are claimed or could be claimed for federal income tax purposes as a dependent by this sponsored non-citizen's sponsor or the sponsor's spouse, used to size the sponsor's tax household in sponsor income deeming (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 2, b).

Fact.Name: Sponsor household size
Fact.Description: The size of this sponsored non-citizen's sponsor's tax household, equal to one (the sponsor) plus one if the sponsor has a spouse plus the number of other people claimed or who could be claimed as a dependent for federal income tax purposes by the sponsor or the sponsor's spouse (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 2, b).

Fact.Name: Sponsor household federal poverty level
Fact.Description: One hundred percent (100%) of the federal poverty level for a household equal in size to ../sponsorHouseholdSize (this sponsored non-citizen's sponsor's tax household), effective October 1, 2025, used in computing the sponsor gross income eligibility limit (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 2, b; 4.401.2). Looked up from the household-size schedule, with /fplPerAdditionalPerson added for each sponsor household member beyond eight.

Fact.Name: Sponsor gross income eligibility limit
Fact.Description: The SNAP monthly gross income eligibility limit for a household equal in size to this sponsored non-citizen's sponsor, the sponsor's spouse, and any other person who is claimed or could be claimed by the sponsor or the sponsor's spouse for federal income tax purposes as a dependent, subtracted from the combined sponsor and spouse gross income (after the twenty percent earned-income reduction) in sponsor income deeming (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 2, b). One hundred thirty percent (130%) of the FPL for the sponsor's tax household size.

Fact.Name: Sponsor and spouse deemed income
Fact.Description: The combined monthly income of this sponsored non-citizen's sponsor and the sponsor's spouse after the two policy deductions in sponsor income deeming: their combined gross income reduced by twenty percent (20%) of their combined earned income (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 2, a) and by the SNAP monthly gross income eligibility limit for the sponsor's tax household (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 2, b). This is the per-sponsor amount, before any division among multiple sponsored non-citizens.

Fact.Name: Sponsored non-citizen count in household
Fact.Description: The number of sponsored non-citizens this member sponsors who are themselves members of this SNAP household, derived as the count of /members whose sponsorId references this member (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 2, c).

Fact.Name: Sponsored non-citizen count outside household
Fact.Description: The number of sponsored non-citizens this member sponsors who are not members of this SNAP household, as demonstrated by a sponsored non-citizen in this household to the local office's satisfaction (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 2, c).

Fact.Name: Sponsored non-citizen count
Fact.Description: The total number of sponsored non-citizens this member sponsors, across all households — the sum of the in-household and outside-household counts. Used to divide the deemed sponsor income among the sponsored non-citizens when the sponsor has sponsored more than one (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 2, c).

Fact.Name: Deemed sponsor income
Fact.Description: The monthly sponsor income deemed to this sponsored non-citizen as unearned income, computed as the sponsor and spouse's deemed income (after the 20% earned-income reduction and the sponsor's tax-household gross income limit) divided among all non-citizens the sponsor sponsors (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 2, c). Zero for members without a sponsor so the value can be added into /members/*/unearnedIncome without making it incomplete for non-sponsored members.

Fact.Name: Actual money paid by sponsor
Fact.Description: The actual monthly money paid to this sponsored non-citizen by the sponsor or the sponsor's spouse, derived as the sum of monthlyAmount across /incomes entries belonging to this member with type SponsorPayments. Used to determine whether any excess over the deemed sponsor income must be added as additional income to the non-citizen (10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 4).

Fact.Name: Effective deemed sponsor income
Fact.Description: The deemed sponsor income share applied to this sponsored non-citizen for SNAP, zeroed when the sponsor income and resource deeming provisions do not apply per 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, E (see /members/*/sponsorIncomeAndResourcesDoNotApply). Otherwise equal to /members/*/deemedSponsorIncome.

Fact.Name: Sponsor income
Fact.Description: The monthly sponsor income considered for this sponsored non-citizen, equal to the greater of the effective deemed sponsor income share (zeroed when the 4.000.1, E exemptions apply) and the actual money paid by the sponsor or the sponsor's spouse. Per 10 CCR 2506-1, 4.000.1, D, 4, actual money paid is not considered as income unless it exceeds the amount already deemed; when it does, only the excess is added to the considered income, so the total considered equals the actual amount paid.
